title: D'Andre Swift, T.J. Edwards reflect on win over Eagles, preview Week 4 | Press Conference
text: when you when you look back on Monday night, like what impressed you most about how Case came in and like ran the offense? >> Exactly what you said at the end, how he ran the offense um from from start to finish uh with Case and uh throughout the whole week, man. Just his excitement that he brought every single day. Um I knew what it was going to look like. Just happy to see him go out there and have that type of game. It it was big for us, but he was great the whole night. >> What did you see in practice that was going to happen? just him being a vet and um the knowledge of the offense um how he was able to operate throughout the week. Um we felt real comfortable as offense going into it. Yeah. >> You feel that way with anybody who's in there? I mean like with Sure. And how have you kind of built rapport? >> Yeah. >> With all all the quarterbacks in that room, we all feel the same way. And I'm sure anybody you ask that will have a similar answer um with how detailed that room is and u their job assignments and how they all kind of control the uh the huddle when they're in there and they had them opportunities. They uh they all do a great job. Yeah. >> How important is for you guys to know what direction they're going early in the week as far as who's at quarterback? >> Uh how important I mean we got a a great amount of belief in any three of them guys. So um outside of everybody else uh kind of we can't control that, but um whoever they put out there uh we have the utmost belief and that they're going to be able to get the job done. >> You played for the Lions. How much did Aaron Glenn drive you crazy during practice? >> Drive me crazy. Yeah, but was just saying like dur train camp. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. For sure. Definitely was talking a lot. Um AG has been been phenomenal and to see him how the Jets team is ascending since he's been over there. It's been good, man. He's a uh great coach. Great coach, very vocal. Um gets after a lot. That's what I remember um being out there in Detroit. But um excited to go against him. >> Andrew, their their run defense is pretty strong right now. What do you see that that makes them difficult? >> Uh they're good at every level. um flash flow to the ball. Um all 11 around the ball all the time. AG being a defensive guy. I know they play with a lot a lot of swag and um he's been done a great job setting that coach over there and you can tell they following him. Yeah. Doing a great job. you guys have have been committed to the run obviously for a long time, but what impact do you see that having even in games where it's not hitting hitting hitting when you just stay with it and then the game you start getting >> we we know that's what teams are trying to look to take away and um shout out to Ben for when it's not really clicking early on for staying with it. Um >> so when they try to take that away and then K's doing what he did um throughout the game and kind of we can win any any way we need to and that's that's the good thing about this offense. as a follow that seemed like a lot more success late versus earlier adjustment wearing them down. How do you kind of >> I would kind of say wearing them down. You got to be able to uh four quarters. It's a long game out there. They did a they had a hell of a plan game plan going into it. They did a good job executing that. Um and like I said, shout out to Ben for sticking with it. We knew we was going to be able to we had to run the ball at the end to kind of sew the game. Um was able to do that. had a pretty good view and a a fun reaction on the quarterback sneak touchdown. What was your uh takeaway seeing it from where you saw it from? >> It was amazing. That's the crazy I think uh that's the first part first play I've been a part of. When we get the they shift and we kill it, get the exact look that we practicing in um in practice or whatever. So when they shifted out, I Yeah. What does that mean when you get a play like that that unfolds the way that the creative minds thought that was going to? >> Shout out to Ben and everybody upstairs that uh that mean that uh it's a lot of film study and um things like that that go into it. They do a great job up there trying to uh well get in every scenario. Defense does this, we have an answer, kill it to this look. Um that that was that was a great one right there. >> Your reaction to kind of the the reaction to you guys beating the Eagles? I know last week you said uh people were counting you out uh as a team before you even started to play the the Eagles. >> That was a big that's a good win for us just because it was the next opportunity on the schedule. Um being able to come back after a week um like we had against the Vikings. Um bad taste in everybody mouth after that one. So being able to come out with a win was big. It just so happened that the Eagles was the next opponent. TJ, how much better do you you feel about the defense, you know, three weeks versus how you guys felt after the, you know, week? >> Yeah. Um, I mean, obviously just that I think for us, like, you know, we came we came out um and just didn't play our best. I don't think anyone did. Um, you know, from top to bottom. And honestly, that's kind of what we're focused on right now is just like how do we get to where we're all seeing the same thing and we're we're all firing on all cylinders and um definitely taking steps each week and yet there's still stuff that we got to clean up and and kind of get right um for these coming weeks, man. But definitely excited just to go out there make some plays like have fun. Felt like we were just kind of flying around and um you know, playing off one another and all those type things. But you know, we're back in it today and correcting those things that we we didn't do so well and um we'll get right back to it. What are pros and thoughts about that? The way he's handled so far. >> Yeah, I would say I think with DA the one thing that like from the jump like he's not going to he's not going to sugarcoat anything to you. Like he's going to be himself um day in and day out and he's going to be the same guy, you know, and you can respect that. I think um coming in and listening to him talk every day of what his expectations are and um what his standards are for what we want to get done and then it's kind of on the players to uphold those things, you know, and um so I think we just respect how he goes about his business um how he tacks each week and how he he expects a lot, you know, and that's that's what you want out of a coach. >> What do you like most about the way he calls the actual game? Yeah, I feel like, you know, early on, especially just kind of going off of like last game, um, you know, they were running the ball really well, so we couldn't really get to some of the things that we wanted to get to. Um, you know, on those third downs and then the second half, we were able to kind of stop the run early on and then kind of, um, you know, dictate the terms in that way and we were able to get in some things that that we were practicing throughout the week. But um you know each week he's got a wrinkle in there that you know you're excited about or um you know you know he wants to be aggressive and you know he wants to dictate terms and um you know as a defensive player like that's what you want. >> Clear once and for all like when you were kind of near that Eagles huddle right before your interception if you uh heard any useful information before you made that interception. >> I did not. Yeah, I didn't hear any useful information. Um, you know, again, like, you know, I know most of those guys, so if anything, I was just getting in there just to see what's going on. And, um, I was just curious, you know, and uh, but yeah, I didn't I don't I don't know what what they were talking about, anything like that. Um, just trying to pick up really anything that I could and um, but yeah, you know, didn't didn't pick up anything useful for sure. >> Are you amazed by how much that's replayed and the speculation about it? Yeah, I think it's more so the camera angle cuz like when I was doing it, I didn't even feel like I was that close and then my wife was showing me after the game I was like I look like I'm off sides. Like um so I think it was more so like the angle of the camera, but to me I was kind of just like leaned over seeing what was going on. But >> is that something you've tried to do in games? >> I I really try to pick up like anything I can throughout the game. Um whether it's like protection or or something like that. But again, at that point too, like um you I knew that they were just checking a lot of things and I was just like leaning over just to kind of see if I could hear anything, you know, um see what Jay Herz was talking about. But yeah, really really couldn't get much. >> TJ, on the topic of takeaways, there was some questions after what you guys did last year on whether you could sustain it. Obviously, it's been good through the first month. In your mind, what are the factors that keep that takeaway total rolling the way you guys had it for the last 20 games? >> Yeah. Um I think the biggest one is just like population to the ball. I really do. I think, you know, even on the fumble that uh book popped out, like that was him hustling to the ball after the play and going to um just take a shot, man. And that's something that we preach. We we show clips every week about those things happening. And um you see it kind of come to life was was really cool. And then again, I think the interceptions are um you know, kind of work hand in hand with with rushing coverage, right? It's bucketing pressure and then it's also being sticky in coverage to kind of make the quarterback get to a second read or force a throw or something like that. And um again, things that we practice and things that we talk about. So for it to kind of come to life is is is really cool. >> When you see Dylan say that Dennis has gotten more aggressive like week one to where we are now in in trying to generate pressure. >> Yeah. I mean I think we're trying to do anything we can to kind of um you know get get the offense you know away from ahead of the sticks. I think anytime it's second and four or you know third and two, third and one that's a tough to live in. Um, so for us, like we really want to win first and second down to so that we can get to our our third down stuff, no matter what that is. Whether that's just playing our, you know, regular four down front and getting to the ball or whether that's, you know, bringing some pressure to try to um, you know, make them think about some things. I think he's done a good job of mixing it up, too. You know, every every play can't be a pressure and every play can't just be um, sitting there seeing what's going on. So, I feel like he's done a good job of mixing it up. >> When you see Dylan and Malik have some success early, what does that do for their confidence, but also the rest of you having confidence in them? Yeah. Um it's it's cool. I think two guys that came in and just just worked. I think Dylan um I was talking about it earlier like just seeing like his pregame like routine like he's running through like a full game, you know, and he's like getting ready to warmed up and he's he's going and I was I was standing by uh before this Monday night game and I was looking at my coach like maybe I need to like up my pregame routine. Like this dude is moving and then he goes out there and flies around. Um so I think he's he's really just came in and like gone to work and same with Malik. I think a like he's from the start made some plays and um also just like good people to be around. I was joking with Malik the other day. He was like, "Hey man, my body's kind of sore." And I was like I was like, "Your body's kind of sore, huh?" Like, "Yeah, I bet." He's like 19 years old or whatever talking about his body sore. But um just really really good kids to be around and um they've helped a lot. We're going to need we're going to need them for sure. >> Dyl Dylan's led the team in tackles all all three weeks. Does that uh I does the linebacker room take that personally? Yeah, I mean it it pisses me off. But um no, I joke with him all the time. He was especially uh you know, week two against Minnesota, he was inserting the box, he's making a lot of plays and I told him I was like, I'm going to start checking the play just so he has to stay high and and get out of the box. But um no, I mean he's again I think with what we do as a defense, we count on everyone to be in their fit and be in their run gap and um he's been a sure tackler, man. He really has. >> The last year and a half, this team's been able to muster response after some tough losses and last week obviously an example of that. What what goes into each week collectively from the head coach down to the locker room that allows you guys to bounce back the way you have? >> Yeah, I think similar to what I was talking about DA about him being the same guy. I feel like Ben does that does that the same, right? And um his expectations are high. You know, he's not going to he's not going to tell any tell you something just just to tell you something, right? He's going to give you the truth, the honest truth, whether it was good, bad, or or ugly. Um but our standards for how we operate, whether it's a win or a loss, it doesn't really change. Um, we come in here, we go to we go to work, we correct what we need to, um, you know, right back to working out and all that today. And then, um, we get on the practice field and just try to improve. Man, I know it sounds whatever, but that's like it's just a day-to-day thing, um, that he's kind of, you know, instilled in this team and, um, that's how we approach it. >> TJ, I know that you don't have to say in who's the quarterback who, but in the culture of the locker room, but a guy performs as well as Case has, is there an expectation or, you know, a nudge uh, toward him? Yeah, I mean I I think for us again like we we don't really know what's going to happen. Um but we're confident in whoever it is. You know, I think all guys in that room have put in a lot of good work and we've seen all of them work and um you know, I was joking uh the other day like uh people were asking me about who's going to be the quarterback for this Monday night game and I was like, it's not it's not going to be me. As much as people were thinking it, um it's not going to be me. Um but I don't know, man. I think we're confident whoever it is and um we'll roll with it for sure. Couple more TJ on on DJ's penalty. Not asking you to fire on the officials, but from a linebacker's lens when you're when you're at the sticks at the sideline, how do you view that on what that whole sequence there and what that was? >> It's tough, man. I think um you know, you we see clips, you know, time after time where um you know, quarterbacks fight fresher yards and uh where they try to to tap on the sideline and um you know, I know I know DJ. I know him personally. We all know him. He's not that type of player that's trying to take a cheap cheap shot or anything like that. Um, we just play hard and I think for him, you know, it looked like he was in bounds and um, you know, he's just trying to take a shot and get him down. You know, you really you really don't know. Those those plays are so tough to kind of judge, especially right, you can slow it down. You can do all those things, but in the moment um, you really don't know unless the quarterback's sliding or something like that. You don't know whether to to pull off or not. So, it's a tough play for sure. Last one. >> Um, you saw Gino Smith last year, he was turning the ball over at a high clip, >> new team, new play, >> that hasn't been the case. What as you go through your early prep, like what sort of stands out with what he's bringing to them? >> Yeah, I think just in terms of his operation, you can just tell they're operating really well at a high level. Um, you know, he's confident in his throws. He trusts his arm. Um, yes. So, I think but I do think just what they do schematically and how they run the ball and um the players they have, the personnel in terms of the speed that they have, it's it's a serious group. Um, so we'll get into it more today, but just in terms of how he's operating at a at such a high level and how their their offense is working well together. Um, that's something that we again want to try to get them off track and make them look at some different things. But, um, it's going to be a real test for sure. >> Thanks, guys. Appreciate you guys.

title: Bryce Young: 'I Have Confidence in Everyone on the Team' | Carolina Panthers
text: Uh, how do you avoid the natural sort of thought that some may have of, hey, we're down some guys on defense. This might be a high-scoring game. Maybe I need to do too much. Like, how do you avoid getting into that that type of mindset? >> Um, well, I trust my guys. Uh, I trust this team. Um, obviously I feel for all the guys that, you know, yeah, that have have been down and just on a personal level, um, I feel for them. Uh, but I have confidence in the entire group. Um, it's a next man up league. You know, obviously everyone knows that. the guys that have been here, the guys that are new here. Um, they put a lot of work in. Um, we're all pros. Uh, again, I have confidence in in everyone on the team. So, uh, yeah, there there's no thought of anything like that. >> What are you seeing early on from this Lions defense? >> Yeah, really good group. Uh, you could tell that they play really well together. They communicate well. They do a lot of different things and for them to do it uh efficiently, not not a lot of busts on coverage, anything like that, um, that that speaks to, you know, their communication, uh, their comfortability with one another. um very savvy players I think at all three levels. Uh they're versatile. Um you know, they've they've been able to play different personnels to uh different personnel on offense and be able to be, you know, fluctuate with their fronts. Um I have a ton of respect for them uh top to top to bottom uh play caller as well. So uh we know it's going to take everything from us and you know right now throughout the week we have to work to put ourselves in position to try to have success on Sunday. Bryce, number one in passing yards per game, fifth in points scored, seventh in total offense. Does it feel like y'all and particularly you are operating at a high level or is it just a question of this is the play call that we're executing and things are coming and good things are coming from that. >> Yeah. Um well, we again I have confidence in everyone on the in the unit um in the team. Um yeah, we we we feel confident in one another. Um but yeah, everyone's just trying to do their job. Um, everyone's just executing. Um, it's it's, you know, Brad doing a great job of, uh, calling plays and and and everyone upstairs dialing it up and throughout the week, us throughout the, uh, throughout the week, um, you know, working to execute and then turning that into Sunday. Um, and also we understand that that doesn't entitle us anything on Sunday. Um, there's it's it's zero zero. That's how it's going to start. Um, when the game starts, we have to go and and establish um, who it is. There's no carryover. Um, so I have all the confidence in the world in this this unit, this group. And really what I love is just our ability to turn the page and know we you know we have to have to execute at a high level um every week in this league. So uh yeah. >> Have you achieved some sort of flow state though like at some point this season so far? >> Um again we we've we've had our highs, we've had our lows, you know, there's been ups. There's been stuff that we we still feel like we want to grow in. Still uh stuff that, you know, we think we can do better. Um and that's the the the beauty of the sport. You know, you're always chasing perfection. Um, that's our mindset this week. You know, we want every play to go out there and be executed at high level. That's going to be the goal. Um, right now we're putting in the work to try to make that possible. >> Hey, Bryce, you showed up um your name showed up in the injury report and just how are you feeling and u ready to go for Sunday night and what kind of happened uh with the injury. >> Yeah. Um feel good. Um blessed um what happened early and finish the game. Uh definitely a blessing. Um and you know it's football that that stuff like that happens again. Um, you know, we're all battling through through something, um, in this sport. Uh, so yeah, um, I'm excited. Um, feel good, practiced. Um, so, uh, obviously I'm not a doctor, but, uh, me personally, I feel good. So, >> you were briefly, did, was there ever a point where you thought you might not be able to get back in the game? >> Um, no. Um, you know, little whatever tape. Uh, again, everyone throughout the game, you know, you you get little stuff that goes on. It's a it's a you know, football is football. Everyone's battling through something throughout the league. So, uh, you know, just get ready to go back out there and go. >> Which knee is it? >> Uh, is that like a injury report thing, but >> uh, well, someone someone got to look it up then. I don't know what I'm able to disclose or not disclose. So, >> okay. >> You can Google it. >> Okay. Um, >> you say you can Google it? >> Yeah, if it's on the if it's on the internet. It's not on the injury report. I just said, >> "All right. Well, then it's just one of the knees." >> Got it. [laughter] >> Well, as as a quarterback, how important is, you know, uh, like having a strong, healthy lower body and not >> not just in your mobility, but also in other parts of the game. >> Yeah. Well, um, obviously everything's important. Um, I I trust in God. Um, you know, all that stuff that's all out of my hands. Um, I I try to walk in faith. Um, I put all my all my trust in that. And also we have an amazing training staff, uh, strength staff. They do all the stuff. So, um, yeah, I'm I always put my faith in the Lord. >> Against the Rams, you guys were in kind of a similar spot. A bunch of defensive guys missing, hurt, suspended, whatever. Does having done that make it easier to do it the next time? >> Um, again, I I think that for us, we're we're we're confident who's in this building. Um, you know, it's always a next man up mentality. Um, everyone works really really hard. I think from the outside, obviously you only get to see a select amount of guys on Sundays, but from the inside, um there's so many people putting putting reps in, um being locked in and focused in meetings, doing a lot of really good things. Um and that that breeds confidence. So, um I don't think we have to pull from anything in the past. Uh you know, this is a new group, a new unit this year. Um but again, everyone works uh tremendously hard. I have all the confidence in the world in everyone. So, uh you know, we're we're excited. First time in 10 years a team has played on Sunday night football. Just as a football fan, is there is there anything to that? Like is it exciting to play on Sunday night and and at what like do you get to enjoy it or are you two sort of dialed in? >> Yeah. Um yeah, certainly a privilege. Um obviously that you know what it comes with. Um the end of the day it's football. Um it's going to be the same goal. Um the calls are going to come in the same, the field dimensions are going to be in the same u it's you know when you're out there it's not going to make a difference. um you know, you're going to the goal is to go out there and execute. That doesn't change. So, obviously embrace the the time change. You embrace obviously, you know, uh maybe a couple more moving parts. Um but, you know, between the lines, we're we're playing football. >> Bryce, about that Rams game that Darren asked you about. That was one of your best games. Did you feel going into that week that you had to kind of take it to another level? >> Uh no. Again, for me, it's about executing the plan. Um uh my trust is my trust is in the the people around me. Um we all just we all just are there to do our jobs. Um there's there's no uh again I trust everyone on both sides of the ball. Um I want to execute at the highest level when when Brad gives me a play in the year. I want it to go the way that you know we talked about on the side. All that stuff. Um there's uh nothing extra. Just trying to execute. >> So in other words, there's no reaper button that you push where you feel like you have to overcompensate. >> Uh no. I I try to do my job every play. That's all. >> How have you been able to really thrive this year despite being pressured more than any other quarterback? >> Um, again, uh, I'm not big on the nextG stats or how they come in. Um, but, uh, I I feel like I have, first off, I have the confidence in the world in us up front in the line. Um, everyone that does our protection work throughout the week, um, [snorts] I have confidence in them. Uh, again, I don't know what the stats say, but we have a we have a great group, and it's not all, you know, it's not all anyone at fault, but also again, that's also a big reason why we've been able to have success. It's not just me back there. Obviously, it takes all 11 out on the field. Uh, I just rely on the guys around me. Um, try to execute a high level. They're doing a great job uh upstairs um dialing up and throughout the week preparing us. Um, and I just try to do my 111. >> Just curious to follow up on, are there any like analytics or stats that you look at and say, you know, is your self evaluating things that you look at and say, "Hey, I need to do this better. Do we need to do this better?" Is there anything you pay attention? >> Uh, yeah. I might I I get a little analytics report of stuff um from uh yeah, little analytics report for stuff other team ourselves, self scout stuff, just trying to improve. Uh shout out to Eric does a great job helping me out with that stuff. But uh um again, it's all just stuff for for me to grow, for us to grow as a unit. Um and yeah, very sweet to week. anything you look at and say look at first and say you know is this important or you know >> maybe but uh I'll keep that one to myself. Yeah. >> Appreciate you guys. [music] [music]

Um, it changes them. It it energizes them and um and really makes them feel a part of what we're doing. Not to say that running the scout team and do that. It's not important. It's vital to what we do. What's the best? down. Hello. 4-hour Rice. >> Uh, how do you avoid the natural sort of thought that some may have of, hey, we're down some guys on defense. Uh, again, I have confidence in in everyone on the team. So, uh, yeah, there there's no thought of anything like that. >> What are you seeing early on from this Lions defense? >> Yeah, really good group. Uh, you could tell that they play really well together. They communicate well. They do a lot of different things and for them to do it uh efficiently, not not a lot of bus on coverage, anything like that. Um, that that speaks to, you know, their communication, uh, their comfortability with one another. Um, very savvy players, I think, at all three levels. Uh, they're versatile. um you know they've they've been able to play different personnels to uh different personnels on offense and be able to be you know fluctuate with their fronts. Um I have a ton of respect for them uh top to top to bottom uh play caller as well. So uh we know it's going to take everything from us and you know right now throughout the week we have to work to put ourselves in position to try to have success on Sunday. >> Bryce number one in passing yards per game, fifth in points scored, seventh in total offense. Does it feel like y'all and particularly you are operating at a high level or is it just a question of this is the play call that we're executing and things are coming and good things are coming from that. >> Yeah. Um well we again I have confidence in everyone on the in the unit um in the team. Um yeah we we we feel confident in one another. Um but yeah, everyone's just trying to do their job. Um everyone's just executing. Um it's it's you know Brad doing a great job of uh calm plays and and and everyone upstairs dialing it up and throughout the week us throughout the uh throughout the week um you know working to execute and then turning that into Sunday. Um and also we understand that that doesn't entitle us anything on Sunday. Um there's it's it's zero. That's how it's going to start. Um when the game starts we have to go and and establish um who it is. There's no carryover. Um so I have all the confidence in the world in this this unit this group. And really what I love is just our ability to turn the page and know we you know we have to have to execute at a high level um every week in this league. So uh yeah. >> Have you achieved some sort of flow state though like at some point this season so far? >> Um again we we've we've had our highs, we've had our lows, you know, there's been ups. There's been stuff that we we still feel like we want to grow in. Still uh stuff that you know we think we can do better. Um and that's the the the beauty of the sport. You know, you're always chasing perfection. Um that's our mindset this week. you know, we want every play to go out there and and be executed at a high level. That's going to be the goal. Um, right now, we're putting in the work to try to make that possible. >> Hey, Bryce, you showed up um your name showed up with the injury report and just how are you feeling and u ready to go for Sunday night and what kind of happened uh with the injury? >> Yeah. Um feel good. Um blessed um what happened early and finish the game. Uh definitely a blessing. Um and you know, it's football that that stuff like that happens again. um you know, we're all battling through through something um in this sport. Uh so yeah, um I'm excited. Um feel good, practiced. Um so, uh obviously I'm not a doctor, but uh me personally, I feel good. So, >> you were briefly, did was there ever a point where you thought you might not be able to get back in the game? >> Um no. um you know, little whatever tape. Uh again, everyone throughout the game, you know, you you get little stuff that goes on. It's a it's a you know, football is football. Everyone's battling through something throughout the league. So, uh you know, just get ready to go back out there and go. >> Which knee is it? >> Uh is that like a injury report thing, but uh well, someone someone got to look it up then. I don't know what I'm able to disclose or not disclose. So, okay. >> You can Google it. >> Okay. Um >> you say you can Google it? >> Yeah, if it's on the if it's on the internet. It's not on the injury report. I just said, >> "All right. Well, then it's just one of the knees." >> Got it. [laughter] >> Well, as as a quarterback, how important is, you know, uh, like having a strong, healthy lower body and not >> not just in your mobility, but also in other parts of the game? >> Yeah. Well, um, obviously everything's important. Um, I I trust in God. Um, you know, all that stuff that's all out of my hands. Um, I I try to walk in faith. Um, I put all my all my trust in that. But also we have an amazing training staff, uh, strength staff. They do all the stuff. Um and that that breeds confidence. So, um I don't think we have to pull from anything in the past. Uh you know, this is a new group, a new unit this year. Um but again, everyone works uh tremendously hard. I have all the confidence in the world in everyone. So, uh you know, we're we're excited. Like is it exciting to play on Sunday night and and at what like do you get to enjoy it or are you two sort of dialed in? >> Yeah. Um yeah, certainly a privilege. Um the calls are going to come in the same, the field dimensions are going to be in the same. Um it's you know when you're out there it's not going to make a difference. um you know, you're going to the goal is to go out there and execute. That doesn't change. Um, there's, uh, nothing extra. Just trying to execute. >> So, in other words, there's no reaper button that you push where you feel like you have to overcompensate. >> Uh, no. Um, everyone that does our protection work throughout the week, um, I have confidence in them. It's not just me back there. Obviously, it takes all 11 out on the field. Uh, I just rely on the guys around me. Um, try to execute a high level. Uh so Eric does a great job helping out with that stuff. But uh [snorts] um again, it's all just stuff for for me to grow, for us to grow as a unit. Yeah, >> appreciate you guys. Yeah, it's very nice.

title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference 9.30.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: tight end is is a is a big deal obviously to you. It's become a bigger deal in the league just having multiple guys that can do stuff. Why do you think that evolution has happened and outside of Trey? How important is what the rest of those guys are doing for you? Yeah, I mean it's um I could you guys want to sit here for 15 minutes and talk about it? >> No, it's a good one because um you know as as uh the the league has evolved by the year and you know defenses are doing whatever they can to limit explosives. Defenses are doing whatever they can to keep a cap on the defense, keep a you know keep an umbrella on the defense if you will and keep everything in front of them and then and then go play fundamentally sound after that. um and and sticking in their shells. Not everybody, but sticking in their shells, not giving quarterbacks tells whether rotation or whatnot. Uh it's in my opinion given way to let's run the ball. Either dink and dunk, keep the ball in play like uh the NerS do and get your yards through yak or or running the football. A lot of different ways of doing that. I think it's kind of going back to trying to match because of what happened last year, particularly in LA, but but with amongst other teams as well. Um, but the teams that don't want to match now, you know, you're a little bit bigger than maybe what they are. And not only that, the teams that don't want to get edged, um, you know, in terms of making you circle the defense, now you're creating an extra gap because you put a bigger guy there as opposed to Marv, Mike, KB, something like that, you know. I didn't think it'd be that extreme, but you knew there was going to be a >> [snorts] >> um a overcommitment to tight ends, if you will. And and I don't know if it's true, but I mean, it felt like it was the most tight ends I'd seen drafted through the first two days. Then I can remember at least being in the league. And again, it was uh it was almost like, oh yeah, no crap. [snorts] >> Appreciate coming somewhere where where it seemed like the Cardinals were ahead of the curve in drafting Tim as a blocking guy in the third round and and obviously getting traded. you you came into a place where there was so much infrastructure at tight end already. >> Yeah. No. Um I hated that they drafted Tip here because we we we loved Tip and uh so you know, particularly being in the division. So now I'm very happy that we have Tip and I'm excited that he is continuing to to progress. Obviously, Trey's, you know, I mean, that's you're talking about the elite of the elite in terms of what he does and um uh you know, obviously you guys see what he does as a as a pass catcher with the ball in his hands, his mindset. Um but what he's able to do in the run game, too, and he's and it's like one thing like like KD's elite and in my opinion a Hall of Famer. Is that what you bring? >> Yeah, I mean there's there's a fine line in my opinion. Here's what our players do well, and here's what the landscape of the league is saying in terms of what you should do against the defenses. So, I know it's kind of a word salad right there, but there's just a lot that goes involved. I know that he's near the top of the league since he came into the league when it comes to interceptions. So, when you go up against a quarterback that's very high risk, high reward type of quarterback, what do you stress on the on the defense? >> Yeah, I mean, you just Well, the same thing you stress every week. I mean, just stick to your keys, stick to your fundamentals, stick to all those kind of things. How did you feel like those guys responded in that first chance? >> Yeah, I thought they responded like um like we thought they would. Um, obviously things always clean up. What's making that possible for him? >> I think he's got I think he's got a mindset for the ball. Um, I think he's uh, he's kind of got that um, like he likes getting grimy. So, um, you know, I I got a lot of confidence in Max. I got a lot of confidence in DB as well. got a lot of confidence in that group and they just got to continue to send. >> You guys are are are facing the highest rate of zone and cover two in the league. Why what's your best guess as toes why teams are trying to do that so much? >> Well, we've played three teams that that's their philosophy and it's like everything right now is it's a mirage. Now Raheem has put his his you know um his little taste on it if you will and and and um you know his characteristics of what he wants his defense to look like but there still is characteristics of the old San Francisco 49ers. So, >> when you look [snorts] at the uh, penalties versus explosives kind of issues, what is more troublesome in your opinion? >> Uh, well, most of the I mean, most penalties for the most like you're not going to be penalty-free post snap.
