You know, it kind of like is what it is. You want to limit it and you want to educate and you want to talk about it, but you also don't want to limit their play style. It's it's the pre-nap stuff that that we need to fix. And we know that. And uh and again, that's not that's not on the 11 players. That's on all of us. And it starts with me. Uh providing, you know, again, the right clarity and confidence that they, you know, they're not, it's just second nature for them. Like we we have to mix up our cadence. We have to it's it's a huge advantage to what you do offensively because it's the only real advantage you have, you know, when you're snapping it. They don't, you know, and so be able to mix that up. And again, the easy answer is, well, just go on the same cadence every time. Well, we're not trying to be middle of the pack. Like that's just not what we're trying to do. Like middle of the pack, you're gonna have someone new sitting up here like and and so like um we're going to be hard on ourselves. We're gonna have a standard. We're not going to be hard-headed, but we're gonna have a standard in which we operate. [snorts] >> Previously, you talked about your offense whenever you in LA kind of developing over the year. How week one didn't look the same as week 18 whenever it came to how you guys ran the offense. Is three weeks kind of enough for you to see like the foundation like the building blocks of what your offense is? >> Yeah, I think >> Yeah, I mean I there's still a lot more time. Uh, I don't believe it's October yet, but don't quote me on that. Um, but, uh, no, [snorts] I mean it's, you know, feel like, um, I know personally I'm I'm getting to know these guys even more from what Sunday's like. I know them very well. Uh, obviously because I'm with them every day, but but you really get to know them in terms of their football character within that three and a half hour window there. So, you know, I think uh us and the coaches and and same with same same thing with the players to us. Like, we're all getting to know each other a little bit more every single snap that we're out there. Offense, defense, special teams, us as a team. So, uh but with that said, I you know, I have yet to be on a team that 3 weeks in, we look the exact same we did um you know, in week 16, week 17. In 2016, I was go the two top offenses that that I've been fortunate to be a part of 2016 in Atlanta. um very much different from week three to the end of the year. And then obviously last year in LA uh didn't have a snap of 13 personnel until um Baltimore basically the fourth quarter and up 10-3 and then um ended up running like 40 snaps of it in uh you know in Europe the next week versus Jacksonville and then it just went you know I don't know what we're going to look like in in you know come week 17 >> with those Go ahead with those quarterbacks that we were talking about earlier. It seems like you've put a lot those outside guys seems like you guys have put a lot on their play in terms of where their help is or maybe not having that help. Has that been intentional? Has it been the teams that you've played against kind of what what's gone into that? >> Yeah, I mean I I think it at times like there's going to be a stressful down for the corners. But when there's not a stressful down for the corners, then there's going to be stress on somebody else. There's always there's always a stressor within a defense. So, I think you uh you know, like I think the easy answer if I'm a a defensive coordinator or speaking for the defense right now as you ask me that question is you got to mix it up. You got to mix it up because these these uh particularly a lot of these offenses and offensive coordinators, if you're not mixing up, they're going to find it, you know. So, um and then once you do mix it up, you know, where's that fine balance between not making it overly complicated for the players so they they can go out and play fast, you know, and every team's going to be a little bit different with that. This is a little off topic. We're doing something around the league. Um, what are your thoughts on the possibility of bringing back challenges for defensive pass interference? >> Oh man, that'd be a throw flag every single time. [laughter] Um, is that is that actually happening? Is that >> Mark? Anything >> rumor? Okay. Yeah. I don't I mean, until that's you know what I I I honestly as as you asked because I haven't heard that and I obviously haven't heard that and haven't thought about that for years, but like it's um I I'd rather not. I think it's very subjective. Make the call, live with the call. You know, we as coaches have to make the call and live with the call. Some are good, some are bad. Same thing happens over there. I respect the job that those guys have to do. So, um I'd rather not, but I'm sure people would disagree with me. I'm sure you were kidding, but if it was brought back, you just f you would throw the challenge flag. >> Well, I mean, it would have to look like DPI. I'm not trying to just blindly throw. >> With with Walter obviously playing inside, it's sometimes hard to get a [snorts] judge on exactly how he's doing. From what you've seen and talking with the coaches, where is where is his game right now? Is he is he doing enough for you guys that you're happy? >> Yeah, he just needs to keep going at it. Um, I love Walt. Um, and he wants it really, really, really bad. And that's what I respect. Like it's I look at people's intentions and I know his intentions are that he wants to help this team and he wants to be productive. So, um, he just needs to keep going. Uh, like I told him today, I said, you know, how many people sacked Brock Pury this year? Zero. So, uh, you and countless others have yet to get to him. And that's a credit to Kyle. That's a credit to their players, you know. So, um, with that being said, we have a high standard. And so we need to, you know, find ways to not worry about what other teams haven't done and we have to do it. >> We've seen during pregame warm-ups, James Connor is very much around the running backs and he's always on the sidelines talking to Jeremiah, Tyler, Bam. What has his mentorship meant to the offensive unit even while he's not out there on the field right now? >> Yeah, he's just he's you want positive energy around you, you know, whether you're talking or not. like you you know when you walk in a room or walk in someone's house and you can just feel that the energy is right. Uh that's what you feel at least me and I know the offense and the team when you walk by him or when he's in the room. So uh he doesn't have to say much to get his point across. And um you know so um I hope he plays for as many more years as he wants to play. One, five, 10, however many years that is. And then after that I would guess he probably wants to get into this in in in some way shape or form. high school, college, pro, I don't know, you know. So, uh, he's a phenomenal human being and his energy's right. >> Coach Brian Burns is out for them obviously, but they have a lot more to offer up front. What about their front seven on defense? >> Yeah, they're they're loaded and and it's uh, you know, you knew that almost last year after the season when when the the cycle was going down and you're like, man, there's a lot of talent over there in New York and uh, and there's a lot of talent on offense, too. And uh unfortunate for them obviously with Brian but but you know um like we always say the show's going to go on and luckily for them they do have a lot of really good players and um Abdul is only getting just better and better. Like he is a problem and he's playing hard and they they got it going right right now and I got a lot of respect for what they're doing. I got a lot of respect for what they're doing schematically. They're they're a sharp operation. >> You obviously talked about Wald a second ago but as a group what do you guys need to do to impact opposing quarterbacks as well? Yeah. And like like I just kind of said, you know, to to Walt, but I'd say to all the other guys like, "Hey, just keep going." You know, it was it was uh one game where we we didn't get to him. I thought I thought that first game, you know, we rushed the passer pretty well. Uh unfortunately for Seattle, we we never had the lead, you know, like it's it's tougher to get to the quarterback in some of those and and they were they it wasn't like they were scatting all five guys out and they were just fiveman protection. They were loading it up. They I'm talking Seattle keepers, play pass, all that where they're in more max protection. uh a little harder to get there and we didn't do our job on offense to allow them to pin their ears back and go and um last week again, you know, kind of buried oursel a little bit. Thought there were opportunities by the way that San Francisco does their offense that uh we need to affect them a little bit more. We didn't. So, here we are and going into week four, put together the best plan. Let's go practice. Let's go detail it up. Uh and then let's get after it on Sunday.

title: Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conference
text: Hey, hey, hey. hey, Heat. Hey, heat. Hey, heat. Hey, hey, hey. Heat up. Everybody Hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey, hey. Heat. Hey. Hey. Hey. [music] Hey, hey, hey. >> [music] >> Heat. Heat. >> Nat. Hey. Hey. >> Hey, Morning. [music] >> Lesser athlete would have fallen. >> I I figured Kevin Sidler is not coming here to be a backup. Is he your new starting record? >> Well, we got to get him into practice and certainly there's going to be a ramp up period for him and as soon as he feels good and ready to go, then he'll be in there. Um what's it do for you as a play caller to go from two look Jagger might be really good players in time but to go from two really young guys who are kind of learning on the flight to having some really veter outs who've done everything in their careers. >> Yeah I think it just calms down the O line like there's a you know when you have veterans in there that have been through the war uh certainly we got young guys playing beside them that definitely can settle things down. So, you know, we're just trying to get these guys integrated. Um, get them up to speed, ramp them up, and, you know, see what they can do. >> That is sounds like Jaden Reed is going to IR. Are you concerned this is a a season ending thing? >> It will be a season ending. >> Yeah, he'll be out. Uh, unfortunately, he let me know yesterday. He's going to have to get have surgery as well. >> Is this about his career? From my understanding, no, but he will be out a significant amount of time. >> How is said, how is he dealing with is dealing with this? >> I mean, it's tough on him. He's a guy that, you know, he he wants to be out there and compete and certainly I think that anytime you go through a situation like that, it's it's a pretty scary deal. I don't I think I may have mentioned this. I I didn't even realize the magnitude at the time, but certainly um when I was out there with them and just seeing what was going on, um you know, it it kind of it shocks you. It jolts you a little bit cuz you you never want to see anybody in that position, let alone one of your own guys, the guy that you have a lot of love for and brings so much to this organization, this football team, to the locker room. He's he's a energy guy and he will certainly be missed. >> Is is it the neck or the upper back or in terms of the surgery or I've seen different. >> Yeah, from my understanding it's it's the neck. I'm not a doctor. I I didn't get into the specifics of it, but um yeah, >> you mentioned Zitler's experience having faced him as a coach. What does he bring to your offensive line from a skill set play style standpoint? >> Yeah, I think everything that you're looking for. He's stout. Um I think he's he's he's can anchor uh in pass pro. He's he's really effective in the run game, whether it's zone scheme, gap scheme, he's done it all. So there's nothing he hasn't seen or done. Um and we just got to get him ramped up. >> Yeah. Yesterday Steno said that you guys have had a lot of hard conversations, productive conversations, but I'll leave it at that. What does that mean as far as the offense goes? Are you guys pondering some significant changes or >> Well, I think you always have an afteraction report, you know, after every every game, every situation. Um certainly we can all improve, every one of us from coaches to players and uh we need we need to improve and in this league you better improve fast. So, we have that urgency to improve and um you know, you always got to look inward I think when you're going through a tough time. >> You're still complex though. >> Yeah. >> Goody was saying this summer that he was worried that if you cut some of your depth pieces on the O line that other teams would claim them. Um what happened with maybe your evaluations of where the O line was at now that you need to make all these signings three weeks in? Well, I think as you go through um you know, sometimes I think practice the way teams practice in the league um it's a lot different than than the game. And uh when you get into game action, I think that's when you get a real evaluation of of everybody. And by no means are we dismissing these guys that have have played for us. I think they're young players. they've got a long road ahead of them um in regards to but but we got to get improvement as well. So I think we felt like it was a necessary step that we had to take. >> Hey Matt, do you um have you considered or do you need to move Adam Stanovich to full-time O line coach? >> Uh he he spends a lot of time in the O line room, but to say that we need to make him the full-time O line coach, I'd say no. >> How come? >> Uh because I got a lot of confidence in the guys that we have. I mean, not to reflect on the past, but you know, we've had a lot of success in that room in prior prior years, and unfortunately to this season, we we haven't done it. But, um, it doesn't change the way like it's not like we're reinventing the wheel in terms of how we're coaching, what we're coaching. We just haven't been productive. And I think we all take a fair share of blame in that in terms of what schemes are we putting these these players in. And then ultimately they've got to go out there and execute. But certainly we got to ask them to or we got to put them in a position where they're capable of going out there and executing to the level that we need to win football games. >> Matt, you have a quarterback and two receivers that are very good this season. Even at the explosive play, the protection obviously is not allowing that to be as efficient as you like it to be. the goal to to get it to that point where you can hit more explosives or do you have to scrap that idea for now and try to just do what you can do? >> Yeah, I I think it's always you got to do what you can do. Um it's what do you have to do to win football games and that could change on a week- toeek basis depending upon, you know, what you're seeing, what you're facing. If you're seeing a ton of pressure, you might have situations where you got to get the ball out of your hands. And you know, um, guys got to break a tackle, make a play to get that explosive gain. And then there's other situations if if um, you're rushing four or whatever and you're you're holding up in protection, then you can take your shots. But I think it's everything has to play off one another. And I, you know, the run game's got to play out the pass game. We hadn't been running it very well. Um and so we need all all areas got to improve. >> Back to Jill asking because we all know him. Um how do you how on earth do you replace what he does on the field? >> It's tough. I mean like I said he he brings so much and and the versatility and how we use him and just all the different roles. I I would say it's going to be by committee. You know, there's a lot of things that the other guys can do as well. I mean, we're we're integrating Sky Moore into some of that stuff. Bo Melton, um Jay Mike, all those guys are going to have to share the load >> and determining when Zeitler can play or where Tomlinson and Beckton fit along the offensive line. What are these next couple days of practice look like to try to find those answers? Yeah, I think that's we haven't even set foot on on the grass with them, but we have a plan in place and we're going to follow that plan and and try to push and try to get these guys, like I said, up to speed as as quickly as humanly possible so that they can go out there and contribute. >> Veterans that you brought in all predominantly play guard, right? Is that an indication that when you look at the mentality of the offensive line, it's it's the guard play specifically that's got to improve first. Do you feel like you're in a better position at tackle than center? >> Um, I think I would say it it's we've had four guys that are probably just don't have a ton of starts under their belts in in their in terms of their respective positions. So, just to pinpoint one position, I don't think that's necessarily fair. Um, I think they're all battling and um, unfortunately it's just like you plug one leak and then the next play there's a leak somewhere else. So again, it always starts with us in terms of the scheme and what we're asking these guys to do and how can you alleviate some of the pressure on those guys because they've been put in some tough positions I'd say up to this point. >> You mentioned incorporating Sky on offense a little more with Jay Reed out. Could that affect his role in the return game at all? >> No. >> What are the challenges and preparing for to face a quarterback who doesn't have much of a track record, at least in the NFL level? >> Yeah, there's just not a lot of tape out there on them. So, um, and you don't know what exactly they're practicing. Obviously, you've seen all the preseason tape and I thought he played really well in the preseason. He showed he can beat you with his arm, with his legs. Um, they they implemented a little bit of zone read. Um he's got a live arm, man, and and he's not afraid to let it rip. So, we're going to have to do a good job of of trying to corral him as best we can and um because he's slippery in and out of the pocket as well. And he's a tough guy. He he doesn't slide a whole bunch. >> Will you work in a right tackle? >> I would say that the whole thing's pretty fluid right now. Matt, when you think about all the different pieces that have come in, offensive line, you know, the this preseason moves with Mark and Jonathan and all that, how difficult is it for you or just the coaching staff to kind of shuffle those pieces to hopefully make it work, you know, really early on in the season? >> I think as a coach, you're always problem solving and that's just the nature of the beast. And to say it's difficult, it it doesn't matter at the end of the day. We just got to get to be competent on the offensive side of the ball and be able to move the ball and score points. That that's our job. So, you know, there there's a lot of problems you're always trying to solve and that's that's the way I look at it. >> What's the uh kind of the mood of the team? You didn't obviously get off to the start you're looking for. What do you think of your guys are feeling? >> Yeah, I think the guys came in, you know, that's one thing we talked about is just having attacking it with great energy level and positivity. And I think that's what we're built like in that locker room. And that's a testament to the guy's character. And we're just going to attack it head on. You know, ignore ignore the noise. Uh focus on us and just try to get a little bit better each and every day. >> Good. Thanks, guys.

title: Klint Kubiak and Kirk Cousins Presser - 9.30.26
text: All right, guys. Uh, so Stokes is full go today. Jackson will not practice and Aiden is not here today. Hope to have him back by the end of the week. We'll take any of your questions. >> When Kirk first got here, he said he played some of his best football with you and your system. after these first three games, is this the Kirk that you exactly expected to see? >> Uh he's playing really well for our team and that's what we signed him here to do. You know, he's uh he's leading our team and uh it's three games into it. We got a long season ahead, so we got to play great every week. >> How much does he How much of a runway does he give you as far as maybe being more patient with Fernando's development, the better perk plays? >> Yeah, uh we're just worried about, you know, playing the next game and uh he's playing this next game and Fernando's ready to go when called upon. Do you have a specific timeline for JPJ? >> Uh we just keep getting them healthy and and hope to get him to some practice reps this week so he can play. >> Clint, obviously uh it's just going to be October by game day, but does this feel uh at all like it's going to be a playoff atmosphere, a little extra excitement surrounding a matchup like this? >> I think uh our team, we take every game in that same manner. You know, every game is a is a oneame Super Bowl and this is the best of the best competing against each other every week. So, uh, this should be no different than week one or week 17. >> You, this team has scored 25 plus points in three straight games. It's been quite some time since they've been able to do that. Why do you think this you guys have been so successful putting points on the board? >> Uh, got a lot of great turnovers, got great field position. So, credit to defense and special teams. >> Clint, have you instilled the belief, you know, that, you know, they they haven't won much around here, but in the second half down double digits to kind of still believe and and come back the way they did. How do you instill that? How is that a part of the culture? >> I think our players want to win. You know, we got players that want to win, we got coaches that want to win. Uh the whole organization's on the same page and uh it's three games. It's a three game sample size. So, um we have to just stay focused. >> What do you think is the most valuable thing that Conor Haywood brings to your offense and also this team? >> Um just, you know, the fullback position is a key position on our team. A guy that can play special teams, all four core. He can protect. He can clean up things in the run game. Um he can fit in at running back if needed. So the fullback's has to be a very versatile player. That's what Connor is. >> Brock getting AFC offensive player of the week. What does it say about him that he can miss time and come in and make that kind of impact? >> Uh yeah, really great performance by him. Um but he didn't do it alone. His teammates, defense getting the ball back, um protection, you know, every it's a team effort. All those awards are team awards. uh because you normally don't get them unless the team wins. Um so uh but I think Brock is very studious. He works hard at it and it is it's not easy to to go play a game where you don't have all the practice reps, but says a lot about how smart he is. >> How does how does Brock's skill set from you know traditional tight ends? >> Um you know Brock's a really good player and we need we need all 11 to play really well. So uh he had a really good game. Proud of him, but um he has the full attention of of the Chiefs. So, uh, we need everybody to contribute. >> You mentioned before the season to ride for the brand and play with shock and effort. Are you seeing that and how much more can you get out of that? >> I think that's just things we look for each week, each day in practice and if we do it in practice, then we can do it in the game. >> You saw what Cody White could do in Seattle and getting the call up here. What was it like to give him the call up? >> Um, he earned it. He earned it. >> The Chiefs leading in yards after catch. How do you guys focus on that in practice this week? Yeah, a really really talented team that we're playing. Um, and it's just it's your fundamentals since April. If you if we weren't stressing it in April, then it probably wouldn't show up now. So, the things that we stressed in April, we keep stressing. But, um, this is a very talented team that we have to get on the ground. >> What impresses you most about Kenneth Walker. >> Uh, big play ability. He can hit a home run from anywhere on the field. >> You mentioned the turnovers and the field position, also the fewest penalties in the league. Um, I guess is that what you wanted the identity of this team to be and what you what what do you attribute those things to? >> I think every week you're you're uh you're working on your identity and then someone takes away your identity, takes away something you're good at. So you got to find multiple ways to win and that's what that's what good teams do and u you know you got to win on all three phases in order to in order to win especially against a great team like this. >> Some personnel changes for Kansas City's defense but obviously Spagnolo still there. Kind of what stands out to you about this year's defense so far for them? Yeah, every year just I'd say they're say they're the best coached unit in the league. Shows on tape. >> DJ kind of been quietly doing his job. What have you seen from him and what has impressed you about him? >> Uh, I think what you said is consistency. Uh, doesn't miss practice. Um, very intelligent, always available, and u, he's a guy we really count on every week. >> Max and Mahomes have met quite a few times. What makes him valuable against a quarterback like Patrick Mahomes? Uh, you know, Max would be valuable for for any team, you know, the the way the effort that he plays with in the run in the pass. Um, so he's a major asset to our organization. >> Zeke Masses was making plays throughout the offseason and now we're seeing that playmaking ability translate. What would you attribute that success to? >> Um, I would just I would say number one is he's a competitor, very competitive young man. um sees the game very well and he's got he's got two starts under his belt and getting ready to play a very good offense. So um he's going to get their best. >> Having um coached Kenneth Walker before, especially when he won obviously you guys won the Super Bowl and he was MVP and he the way that he is playing up until this point in the season. Does it give you I guess a little bit extra confidence knowing that you know him really well and playing against a guy like that? Um, you know, Kenneth is is a tremendous back. He's playing as good as anybody in the league right now. And, uh, you know, we have to stop him. He's he's a really good player. >> Thanks. >> Thank you. had good good test this week. Um had a good morning of preparation here. Uh a lot to cover. Um but it's a great challenge, you know, against a great football team. Um, so excited to be back in front of our fans for our second true uh home game, not counting the preseason, and uh looking forward to uh to Sunday. So, take any questions you have. >> Kurt, what would you say is Clint Kubak's greatest strength as a play caller? >> Um, it be hard to pin down any one trade. I think he's organized. Um, I think it it doesn't feel um uh scattered, you know. It feels like it's an organized plan. and I don't get surprised. Um, feel like we're on the same page. Feel like he gets the play calls in quickly. And I only say that not really off the sample size of the last three weeks, but more off of 2021 and even him being my quarterback coach in 19 and 20. Um, and I just appreciate that organizational skills, but also the uh desire to continuously improve. I think at times um you know we come back from a win and he doesn't allow the outcome of a win to cause him to let his guard down on things that need to be coached hard and that's comforting for me because I love you know kind of feeling like nothing's going to get past his uh his watchful eyes. So um I think there's a a kindred spirit there from a you know continuous improvement mindset and um that gives me peace. You >> you've been called a bridge quarterback. Has that really fueled you coming into the season? >> I don't know what I've been called or not. I kind of just insulate. So, uh, that's the first time I've been told I've been called that in terms of I don't I don't know what I've been called or not called. Uh, I like to just stay ignorant and, uh, I just know that I got to know the first and second down game plan today and execute it the best I can on Sunday and, uh, kind of go from there. >> Is this at all a measuring stick matchup, you think? >> Uh, I think every game is, honestly. I mean, last week was a measuring stick matchup. the Chargers is measuring stick matchup. Um it just feels like every week, you know, they're all their own entity. They're 17 separate challenges and you just go out there and do the absolute best you can. Um and and and we look forward to playing a really good football team. It's a great challenge for us. >> Probably don't have to name a whole lot of names beyond Spagnola when it comes to defensive minds in this league for a long time. What's it like from a quarterback's perspective kind of playing chess with a guy like that? >> Yeah, I think you just want to be prepared. Um, you know, I think he's got he's got a great scheme. He coaches his players well. I think they play fast because they know what he wants to accomplish and um um you know, he's done a great job for a long time in this league and uh u have a lot of respect for him and and it's always a challenge going against him. >> You throw out what he's done before. How much of a of a balance is that because it's always going to be new almost on a weekly basis? Yeah, I think I think you study the best you can and and you are aware that um at any time any coach really can throw you a curveball and so that's why you have to know not just the opponent but know your own system and and be aware of you know on the unscouted looks you know what's my answer so that's all part of the preparation each week and um it's a big part of this week. >> What do you think what do you think separates Brock from maybe like traditional tight ends that play the position? >> Well, I think Brock's just a very capable tight end. And I think he um you know is tremendous after the catch with the football. I think he's got a great ability to adjust to the football. Strong hands, good play strength. Um you know there's a lot of intangibles too uh with his intelligence and his work ethic, the standard he holds himself to. You know he's a great teammate. So um there's so many traits you look for in a player specifically at the at the skill positions, the receiver positions like tight end and wide receiver. And um you know he's checking so many of those boxes. There was one uh play back shoulder throw where he worked his way back to it. How do how are you guys able to have that chemistry when you know admittedly you didn't have as many reps as you wanted to with him? >> Yeah, I mean certainly we're still building that. I don't I don't think that it's something that I feel like I did with you know Justin Jefferson and Adam Thielen after playing with them for three or four years. You really you really knew you know what what their game was. because I think we're still developing. But um I remember throwing a back shoulder to Justin in Houston in his maybe second career game, second career start and um late in the game, you know, threw him a back shoulder and he adjusted and I thought, well, I don't know that we have chemistry, but sometimes when you play with really good players, it looks like you have chemistry because they're just that much better at adjusting to a throw and making the play. So, um some of that's probably true, too. But, um every play you're in there together, you you learn more and um I think it helps you then be more efficient moving forward. What do you think the key is going to be to get the running game going at at a little bit of a higher clip? >> Yeah, and I I think it's important uh to stay with it and um you know, I think this coaching staff, this system has done a good job of staying with it and um and I think the more at bats you get also, it gives you more opportunities to not only potentially hit one, but also keep improving as a unit and um you know, and handling all the different looks you're going to get. So, we'll stay the course and uh um you know, I'm confident that u that we'll be happy with our run game as the year goes on. >> When you're playing well like like you are right now, what are sort of the characteristics of your play that stand out to you? Like is it anticipation, reading the defenses? Just kind of what what do you sort of describe to explain, you know, the success when you're in a group like this? >> Well, I think quarterbacking is all about um you know, first of all protecting the football, but so much of it is team. You know, I think you got to remember that, you know, some of our fourth quarter success against the Saints is because our defense was giving us such short fields and getting us the ball back and so they they put the wind at your back and I don't know that, you know, suddenly we as an offense were playing a totally different game in the fourth quarter. It was just that we were get put in a great position by our defense. So team always helps, you know, and then the guys around you um always helps. But um it's really your unit, you know, when the quarterback's playing well, I'm sure the unit's probably playing well also. So, we all kind of feed off each other and it goes both ways, but um protecting the football will always be really important at this position. >> Did you know uh during those two years in Atlanta dealing with some injuries that you still had this level of play within you? >> Well, I I think you just I mean going back to even before tearing my Achilles, you know, your level of play is week to week. I mean, you basically feel like hey, I don't there's no guarantees that next week is somehow going to be um you know, at the level I want it to be unless I go out and go earn it and go do it. So, that's the great part about this league is you've got to go out every single week and prove it to yourself, prove it to everyone else. Um, and so I've never really felt like, you know, anything was going to be handed to me or given to me. You got to go out and play at that level. And I think the opportunity, you know, was what I was more interested in was just having an opportunity to go see. Um, but you got to go do it. >> As a quarter, as a veteran quarterback yourself, what's the biggest challenge that someone like Patrick Mahomes poses this week? Well, I think he's certainly fun to watch, you know, and uh um sets a great standard for quarterback play across our league and um you know, if if they were to, you know, put up a lot of points, then you know, you got to you got to keep up. You also know that um if if you were to get ahead that no lead is safe. Um you're just aware of how capable they are any moment of scoring points and and um and and make it hard on you as as a team. So, there's a lot of respect there and u they've proven it and earned that over many years. and um you know it'll be a great challenge for all of us on Sunday. >> You're the you're the first quarterback in NFL history to have three touchdown passes in the first three games with a with a team. >> What do you credit that to and kind of what comes to mind when you hear that? >> Yeah, again I go back to kind of I don't get three touchdown passes in these games without our defense, you know, getting the ball back to us, giving us short fields, giving us extra possessions. Um, you know, I think our coaches have designed plays that have gotten people open and given us those opportunities. Players have gotten open themselves and done their part and made plays. So, it's really a combination of a lot of factors. Um, you know, certainly I got to do my job, my part, but that's really all it is. It's just a part of it. And any notable accomplishments or whatever you want to to call them, you know, whether it's Brock being AFC offensive player of the week or last week, I believe Zeke was maybe defensive player of the week. any of those are really team awards and um it's a reflection on everybody and the contribution they're making to help that happen. >> I'm sure you saw Case on Monday to show out. You obviously you're having a great start to the season. Matthew Stafford MVP at your guys' age. Just kind of what it says about the wisdom that maybe you know the experience that comes with you know at this point in your career and and kind of how that's maybe propelled your success early on. >> I was really happy for Case. Um you know he played awesome. Uh, no surprise. You know, he's always been a guy who steps up to the moments and and makes plays. Um, you know, I think football as a quarterback, you're only getting better as you get older in terms of knowledge of the game and understanding of all the intricacies of facing defenses and protections and route adjustments and you just keep accumulating knowledge and that makes you a better quarterback. The key is that your body, you know, can keep up as well. And I think as long as uh we can do that, I I I think I actually kind of like myself more at at an older age than a younger age. I'm much better uh much better command at 38 than 28. Um and so that's why the physical is so important. And when you feel like you have that, you start to say, why not, you know, why not uh the older guys at at 38? Because you kind of checking all those boxes. >> In your 40s. >> I'm I'm one day at a time right now. I think I I can't even go past, you know, this week, but uh uh you know, he can circle back in February and we can chat. >> All right. Thank you.

title: Can the Lions’ Offense Keep Scoring as the Defense Improves?
text: [music] And we are live. It's Lions Collective. We're live every single Wednesday at 6 PM. I am your host, Jeff I Freddy. Check me out Wward Sports Crunch host. To my right, uh Justin Rogers, Detroit football network. Below him, Colton Pouncy from the Athletic. And then to the left of him, Will Birfield 97 won the ticket. fellas. Uh before we get into the topics, uh the turnover thing we have going on here every I cannot wait who we chose we choose today. I mean this is one of the most looked forward to things for me when I'm watching Lions games CUZ YOU JUST DON'T KNOW IF IT'S GOING TO happen or [laughter] not. That's it's so much fun. It's great. But we got a lot to get into today. >> JR, you should have gone back to the Chuck Clark. >> I know. I know. He he carried me carried me through the day week one. But uh now who knew who knew that man was going to produce so many turnovers? >> Yeah, Chuck Clark again came in clutch. And uh we'll talk about that defense of courseing in the offense. We'll talk to Blake Miller today and then we'll get on to our dog and and pony show picks. Let's talk about that defense because uh when you check ESPN, you see Gino had like six incompletions and you know you're if you didn't watch the game, you're like, "Well, there they go again." You know, Gino Smith 90% completion percentage, 350 yards. But at least watching the game, I think a lot of people felt the same way. Um it it's hard to convince people it looked better, but it actually did look better. Guys just didn't make plays, which is something that isn't Kelvin Shepard's fault. But what was kind of your guys' um analysis on the game defensively and and and you know, I know they responded with guys just didn't make plays, but what was your guys' takeaway from that defense on Sunday? >> Really encouraged. And I I preface that comment with it is the Jets, right? like at at some level you have to recognize that, but it's not like the Jets are devoid of talent, right? Like Bree Hall, good running back, top top half of the league. Garrett Wilson is a I would call Pro Bowl caliber receiver. Sadique is going to be a dude in this league. And and Gino's a good quarterback. He's not a great quarterback, but he's been to a couple Pro Bowls. He's accurate. He's obviously king of Ford Field, it feels like, uh, over his career. And so, um, it was a good test. And and when I say encouraged, starts with a run defense, you know, like that that was a team that as as Kelvin Shepard put going into the week, they run the ball, run the ball, run the ball, and when you think they're not going to run the ball, they run the ball again. Uh you shut that down largely over the course of the game and you get through three quarters of it and you've held them to two points and under 200 yards. Like that's that's tracking toward a good day at the office. Obviously, it it fell apart late a little bit, but when you look at why it fell apart, uh feels like the corrections are getting more obvious and easier. You're seeing less coverage bust. You saw a couple man-to-man losses with DJ Reed against Wilson, which at some level are going to happen. Uh I had I had a good talk with DJ Reed uh today in the locker room, and he kind of detailed what he did wrong. I think you appreciate a veteran like that is accountable that is able to see what he did on a mistake perspective and and know what he needs to be better at. Um and then there was the 47 49 yard 43 yard whatever it was pass to Sadiq where it was a zone bust right and and they've had those all year. Uh they've they are more of a zone team now. We've talked about that, but you didn't see the number of zone busts that you saw in those first few weeks. They're starting to clean it up. They're starting to understand their rules. I talked to some of the players that were involved in that this week and kind of was trying to figure out what went wrong, why it went wrong. They were a little light on details even though it wasn't recording, but they know what went wrong. they know what they're supposed to do and they've put in a fix for that specific play because you know that high low concept's going to come on them again. >> Yeah, overall I was pretty encouraged by what I saw. Um you know I think you know there are going to be lapses with this defense um when you're lighter on town in the secondary and you don't have your dudes back there. I totally understand that. But I did think like you have like Chuck Clark has played a lot of football. Like some of these guys that are out there in the secondary, they didn't just forget how to play football. I just think they've had a rough couple of games. Um, and you know, they had that extra time, you know, the mini buy after the after the Thursday night game to kind of correct some of that stuff. And I did feel like it was a little bit cleaner. I think in a game like that, when you stop the run the way the Lions did in that game, um, 3.1 yards per rush, that was the sixth lowest in week three. Uh, I think 26.3% of, uh, rush attempts went for zero or negative yards, that was the fourth highest in week three. Like they they were doing work against the run. So I think the Jets kind of pivoted and, you know, they're trailing. It's like, okay, we're just [snorts] going to take what the defense gives us. So, a lot of, you know, dinking and dunking in that game. Um, now you did have some explosives, but I think that was more losing one-on- ones when the ball was in the air versus, you know, anything else. Um, but I thought like when you defend the run as well as the Lions did, you forced the Jets to kind of be onedimensional in that pass game. I think that's what they were doing mostly. And with that, they were still getting pressure on Gino. They were blitzing a lot less than they normally do. I have some numbers here. >> Lot less. >> 13.6% blitz rate in week three. I believe that was 28th uh in week three among teams that was at 39% in weeks one and week two. So a lot more selective with those blitzes. I think you saw that at that, you know, the final defensive play of the game when Chap did dial up the blitz, the double A gap blitz, and you have, you know, Chuck Clark kind of showing his hand a little bit too early. Uh kind of walking that back and then coming back and blitzing. Um, I don't know if it was the best executed blitz, but I think the goal in a situation like that when you're being more selective blitzes [clears throat] is that when I do call this, it's going to be the right call at the right time. I'm going to confuse somebody. And the Jets had a backup left guard in the game. And I think, you know, he probably didn't know his assignment and you come right at him and and they don't pick it up and you win the game off that play. You secure the game off that play. Um, so I thought Chev was a lot more selective with those blitzes. wasn't just blitzing for the sake of blitzing, which I thought was kind of what they were doing in weeks one, week two. Um, so I love that they were kind of a little bit more selective with that. Um, but yeah, I mean, the run defense making them onedimensional. I know the numbers are what they say, 31 to 36 for 321, you know, all the touchdowns and whatnot, but I think in a game like that, I can live with that. If you're defending the run and making them truly onedimensional the way that the Jets were in that game, make make them beat you in the air, and they were they were making plays. That's going to happen in the NFL. But um if you can hang your hat on run defense and getting that constant pressure, which as we've seen with this defensive line, seems like they're ready to go this year, you know, you can take, you know, some of the lapses in the air in the pass game, I think. So, I was overall pretty encouraged by what I saw. >> Hey, Will, really quick, Colton, do you do you have anything on the completion percentage above expectation? And I know that kind of falls in your your purview of stats you look at, but I I obviously I'm thinking about the the Sadique touchdown, which was an unbelievable throw and catch that I think doesn't get completed probably 85% of the time in this league, but like I I thought I heard something like Gino was way over expectation. >> Well, and a Garrett Wilson touchdown catch, DJ. I mean, like DJ Reed's right there on that play, too. And look, DJ Reed is an above criticism, but >> that's a great throwing catch also. Yeah, I mean he got a little out of phase early in that route, but I thought he recovered really well. I didn't I I thought the first pass interference call was legit. The second one there, I didn't really understand, but uh that's that's a classic case of they get paid too. Great player making a great play. >> Yeah, I think Jeremy put it out. Gino Smith produced a 21.1% uh completion percentage over expected versus Alliance. That's the highest of any quarterback this season so far. >> Damn. >> 21% over expectations. So, he was at 86 and math suggests based on where Lions defenders were, he should have been at 65. Like, that's that's a wild wild gap. And so, I don't know. Like I said, I that falls in the encouraging bucket for me. I think Colton talked about it like they had a ton of checkdowns that the Lions were giving them where they were trusting their tackling, which has been really good this season. So again, I I know the secondary is going to be the the thing of critique, but I I still saw more positive signs than negative. Sorry about that, Will. >> No, you're good. I was just doing some math myself. So if we had applied a 65% completion rate to his 37 pass attempts, he goes 24 of 37. And certainly the numbers at the end of the day look a lot different. So yes, it's kind of cliche to say, but at some point and sometimes you do just have to tip your cap to great players making great plays. Colton, you and I are having the conversation on Monday night about the impact of a blitz at the end of a game when a quarterback and an offense haven't seen that blitz for most of the game. Like Tyler, there were the exact reverse happened on Sunday from what happened in week one. In week one, the Lions are blitzing like crazy in the first half. They're sending nickels and corners and safeties and they have Shook and that offense completely offkilter. and the Saints and Shook and they said as much after the game made the adjustments at halftime and prepared themselves for a lot of those cover zero blitzes the Lions sent and by the second half they were no longer on their back foot. They had the answers they needed because they had become accustomed to seeing all those blitzes and like you talk about wanting to confuse the quarterback. Confusion stems from people being unprepared for something or unaccustomed to something. And when the Lions blitz for just the ninth time on the final and most pivotal play of the game, and I think center blitz they hadn't sent yet, even though they telegraphed it, even though Gino Smith knows that it's coming and the running back next to him knows that it's coming, they they aren't ready for how quickly it arrives or um the running back isn't ready for making the decision between either blocking Jack Campbell through one gap or Chuck Clark through the other. Now, if they had dealt with that over the course of the game, they've probably handled a blitz with ease. But it felt like they sprung it, as you said, at the right time, and they still had the element of surprise to work in their advantage, even though it was clear that Chuck Clark and Jack Campbell in his in his prototypical athletic football move stance at the line. We're coming in for a blitz. And that's that's the value maybe in blitzing a little bit less over the course of a game and picking your spot. And not everyone needs to be Brian Flores blitzing, you know, 60 70% of the time. The other thing that that jumps out, Colton, you mentioned the the yards per carry. I think you said it was like 33. And if you limit it to just the running backs, I believe it was 27. And that that was how the Jets had almost gone 2-0 through two games. Obviously, the run defense had been good, but also they they have been able to sit on the ball more than any offense in football. They came into that game again through two games I think leading the NFL in time of possession. Correct. And most of that was because they had just churned out, you know, enough effective rushing yards over the course of the game. The Lions took that away from them and they forced Gino Smith to beat them. And damn near, if he didn't almost beat them, but that's just kind of [laughter] that's kind of what he does at Ford Field. But um I I want to mention a few players here. I'll just mention one off the top. We can keep batting this round. But, you know, the Lions did talk about and Campbell and Shep each talked about needing to make some some personnel changes after the disastrous two performances in the first two weeks. And they did. And some of those personnel changes showed up in a really big way. And I think the one that could change the outlook of this season most significantly is Andis Raikstraw. Welcome, welcome to the party. Welcome to this defense. And you know, he wasn't the starter. They obviously went with McCreary and McCreary got most of those snaps that had been going to Rocky, but when they went into Nickel, there was Nennis Rickstraw at the outside corner spot and McCreary usually bumped into Nickel. And Nennis Rickstaw took 22 coverage snaps. And if you go back and watch them, almost every damn one was one-on-one, usually backside against Garrett Wilson, who was cooking pretty much everyone else on the field, including DJ Reid, even when Reed was in tight coverage. And when the ball came Wilson's way with Raikstraw there, it was never easy. He made the one catch on third and four on the little out route that Raikstraw was all over. And then Raikstraw had the great pass break up on a second down throw to the sticks. Very similar throw to the out route that Wilson caught where he comes in late and breaks it up. And then he had the huge play in coverage before Chuck Clark's game sealing sack where Wilson runs like a little double move almost like a double move like deep curl and rac with him every step of the way and it just going back and watching him it reminded me of why the Lions were so bullish on the idea that Racer Draw was meant to be an outside corner. I think a lot of us over the past year pegged him as hey maybe he makes more sense at nickel especially when Terrion was still here. We would ask Dan about that periodically and Dan would say like almost adamantly, "No, we we we think he's an outside guy. We like the stickiness. We like the we like the the physicality." I think And even has some sneaky length to him. Like he doesn't look like a big guy, but he he does have long arms and he's got good closing speed. And all of a sudden, maybe the Lions discovered a a CB2 that can really help them this season. I think, you know, there's there's still a need for a CB1, whether it's Reed elevating his game or the Lions looking elsewhere, but you start looking at how emergences in week three could change the season. I think NS RS showing up for the first time in a big way is is really impactful. He played on Sunday half as many defensive snaps as he had played in his NFL career and he did not he did not look out of his depth in in the least. And you know, I asked him after the game, you know, what do you feel like you learned about yourself today, if anything? And he said, I learned that I can play in this league. And it wasn't a realization. It was it was confirmation. He said that he needed that he could go out there backside against a guy making huge money, making huge plays, and and mostly shut him down. And um you know, he went on to say, I think the last thing he told us in that scrum was that's what I got drafted for. And it was like this sort of eureka moment. Yes, even though it happened three years later and you haven't made a real impact on this team yet. Yes, that is what they drafted you for. So, I'm really intrigued to see how it looks in in week four. And, you know, part of that might depend on whether this is going to be a zone defense. I think if it's more of a man defense that probably benefits raw, that's why they drafted him because they felt like he fit their their man scheme. But, man, that's that's major for this defense, that discovery if it continues. And last thing we were talking to him again today and you know I think it was you Dave and I were were hanging around his locker and just kind of hitting him again on the idea that he's maybe arrived now and he wouldn't go that far like he didn't want to say he's satisfied but he he did make the point like I'm a I'm I'm technically a rookie. You know I'm I'm 24 and based on snaps played and games played I'm technically a rookie. So I feel like I got a lot of room to grow. And that's the optimistic view that you know the Rosie view on a on a discovery that could be pretty impactful this season. >> You want to talk about Izzian or you want to talk about Naski Colton? I'll take the other. >> Uh you can talk about Noasi. >> All right. >> I can talk about Izzy. >> Hit us on some Izzy facts. >> Uh I loved his game. I mean like when they brought him in, you know, he had this versatility, you know, being with the Bucks of playing both safety and nickel. Like I think he can be a decent nickel. Obviously he's a he's a big dude. He can tackle. he's well built, you know, but um seeing him at safety and kind of moving around like that was cool to see, man. Like I think he had three tackles for a loss, 11 total tackles. He was all over the field. And you know, I remember a couple weeks ago I was at his locker. This is kind of when he missed, you know, a little bit of time. And I was like, "Hey, you feeling good enough to go?" And he was like, "Yeah, yeah." That first game was just precautionary. I'm ready to go. And I think it was it made its way to Twitter and everyone's like, "Who the hell is Christian Izzy and he's not going to help our defense? What are we doing? What are we doing talking about this guy?" probably weren't saying that on Sunday because he had a really good day. Um and so that safety position obviously is in a bit of flux. Uh did see Brian Branch, you know, walking around practice, still going to need some time, but um you know, guys are dropping and Izzian still standing and you know, he had a really good day was all over the field making plays. Um probably sign of things to come. I think he can continue this level. I I thought it was a really underrated signing when they brought him in after watching his tape and even seeing him against the Lions in, you know, some of those games over the years. Um, so I think he's a good good fit for this defense, good fit for what Shep wants to do. He can blitz, he can tackle, um, you know, he can cover with some of these tight ends and Nicholls. So, uh, good addition. I think it's fan off early on the season. I walked by Brian Branch in the locker room today and I don't I don't know if either one of you guys want to weigh in, but like I think sometimes when you have a leg injury, you hit the upper body a little harder because that's what you can work out. >> I feel like he looks bigger. >> I've been saying yes. >> Okay, so I'm not alone on this. Like it looks like when he's going to hit a he kind of looks like a small linebacker right now. >> I was still think that. Yeah. >> I mean hopefully that didn't cost him his man-to-man skills. But uh on Andis, I'm I'm really curious where the role goes. Uh Dan says more snaps. I wonder given I thought McCreary kind of struggled a bit in this one. Gave up six catches on six receptions. Uh had two of the three uh zone busts that come up in my my brain off the top. Uh I I I wonder if that means that they're going to go more and on the outside in non-nickel packages versus just bringing him in and the nickel uh going forward. Um it's it's really easy to root for the kid uh just given what he's gone through and kind of his mindset and attitude through the whole thing. And you know, it's a small sample size. Like I'm not I'm not going to be the guy that throws him a parade. It was a really really great performance. Uh and and we'll see where it goes from here. But that that's a really nice building block for him. Izzian, man, like I can't even say controlled chaos. Like he was just chaos out there. >> Yeah. >> And sometimes that chaos was really negative and he was in the wrong spot at the wrong time or blew kind of a coverage and maybe some of that got covered up. Sometimes it didn't. Sometimes he was in weird run gas. But like he made a lot of positive plays. And I said this to Will today. It was it was like a lack of energy that they had on defense that like a Alex Analone or a Brian Branch brought that, you know, just can kind of elevate the mood of everyone when you know this guy's flying through gaps when he's blowing up an offensive tackle on a screen in one of the I don't know. It was one of the funniest plays I think I've I've seen in a while where you got this what do we think he weighs? 200 205. Like he's he's a rock solid muscle-wise, but like that's 330 lb uh Missouri offensive tackle out there and he's he's just tossing him like Malcolm Rodriguez tosses guards. And so uh you know, I think you really appreciate that energy. And and the the third defensive change that the Lions made, I think maybe the one we didn't see coming was Trevor Nosk's big workload increase. And I know I I kind of had pitched maybe reducing what Devin White was doing. I didn't think Deon White was playing particularly well. Uh I kind of wanted to put those snaps on Malcolm Rodriguez. I thought that was logical since they were already kind of time sharing. And really they kept the time share and subbed out White with with Noki. And very similar very similar to to Raikstraw. He didn't make mistakes like Noki was all over the place. He was quick to react to short passes. He was filling run gaps with authority. He made tackles and he didn't miss tackles. And I think he kind of perfectly embodied what Dan Campbell talked about when when I brought him up the other day, like he's just where he's supposed to be when he's supposed to be there. And is this Naski's fourth year in Detroit, I believe, and he's he's played over 400 snaps defensively. And sometimes that's a small role where, you know, be it the spy against Lamar Jackson or he's had some spot starts when when guys are really banged up. But I I think this is the first time in his career where he has gotten major playing time because he's earned it. And that's significant. And and he when I was talking to him today, he said, "Guys always told me like this game slows down when when you start figuring it out." And I kept going when when the hell's that gonna happen? Like [laughter] it still feels pretty fast to me. And he goes like this this year like he said like it just suddenly started clicking and he started feeling that sense of it slowing down. And you know there's something to be said about it being more difficult the linebacker position just a so much more mental strain with having to cover the run and pass the way they do. We knew it took Derek Barnes about three years to kind of really figure it out. and Noski came from a far smaller school than Purdue. But um you know maybe it's all just a placeholder to Jimmy Rers ready. And I don't know if that's you know second half of this season. I don't know if it's two weeks from now. I don't know if it's 2027. But Nasi is a guy that maybe we didn't think could help calm things down. But I don't know like again small sample size. Not going to not going to throw a prey for it. like this felt like a guy that could calm things down at linebacker three where they also really needed to find somebody that could do that. >> You talk about the game slowing down for him. The perfect example is the toss play to Bree Hall down by the goal line that Noski was with every step of the way. And you know, he said today and and Dan mentioned yesterday that the coaches have given him that look in practice this week knowing that the Jets had run something pretty similar over the first two weeks. And um you know he yawned. >> Yeah. Well, yeah. He said no yawned at like, "Yeah, no problem. I got that." And you know, he he he figured that the Jets would have identified what he had done on film against Buffalo, which was mostly just lock in on the tight ends and travel with them pre- snap and try and use that to their advantage to get him off the edge and away from the running back. But the Lions were in better communication before the snap on that play. And Nashki read it the whole way. And I was talking to him today and he, you know, so I asked him, you know, when knowing that you had that play and you knew how to stop it, when they ultimately call it and you see it coming, you got to be pretty fired up, right? And he goes, "Yeah, and I know what I look like. Hall probably got it, saw a big white guy and was like, I'm gonna outrun this guy." And I love that because I know I'm athletic and when it comes to a foot race, I can run with the best of them. And he did, dude. He was with Bree Hall every step of the way. I think Bree Hall thought he was going to be able just to turn the corner on him and get to the pylon and he never had a chance. I mean, Noki tackled him out of bounds and I think that was the last snap that Bruce Hall played in that game. He kind of came up lane with a knee injury, but Noki was was was exactly where he needed to be as you said, JR, when he needed to be there. And I don't think they could say the same thing for Deon White. And, you know, I do think they want to get Jimmy Roler more involved on defense over the next, you know, week or sorry, month or or several weeks, but it's not going to be at Noah's expense if he keeps playing like that. Like, he he definitely deserves to be out there. And he did say it felt pretty good. The other funny thing about that that play is um you know Noski said that his rookie season he was matched up in training camp uh in like a one-on-one linebacker versus running backs pass catching drill and he had to cover Jer Gibbs on basically just a go ball and he ended up running with him step for step almost the whole way and he said at that moment I was like oh damn dude I might be able to stick around in this league and Gibbs actually remembered the rep. You know, I talked to him about it today and he was like, "Yeah, dude." I was like, I was I was busting down field and I turned around and this dude's still on me. [laughter] I was like, "What's he what's he doing back here?" So, when Gibb said when when Hall got the toss on Sunday and Noki's out there, he was like, "Oh, Hall's cooked." Like, he's got no chance here. So, kind of cool to see Noah, who's a pretty well-liked guy in the locker room and a pretty humble guy, get get a moment that that he had well earned. Bree Hall apparently didn't look at Trevor Nosky's RA before that game. But but let me remind you height elite. Bench press elite. Broad jump elite. 40 yard 20 yard 10 yard split shuttle three cone elite. 986 can run. >> Yeah, dude. Raz score in my comments. 45 440. >> Okay. Okay. Okay. >> Yeah, he can he can he can move. >> Honestly, I I give the Lions credit for all these changes. Like they could have taken that time during the the mini buy and said, "You know what? We just play Josh Allen and and Joe Brady. We're we're going to be fine. Like it'll it won't always look like this." They could have just said, "Okay, we're going to run it back with Rocky and Devin White and all these guys that were playing early on the season. We'll just we'll just keep them out there. Like we'll we'll figure this out." No, I give them credit for actually looking in the mirror and saying, "Okay, maybe it's time to give some other guys some chances." Um because you have these dudes that are waiting in the wings that feel like they're ready, that feel like they're ready to contribute. You just got to give them an opportunity. They did. They've got way more touchdowns than they do have negative plays on offense, which is four. Purdy himself has accounted for 10 touchdowns, and they have four negative plays on offense. Zero sacks. So, this offense is playing at an absurd level. The question is where the injuries come in. The next question is where the Denver Broncos pass rush, which was so good last year, comes in. And the third question is whatever question you have because I am ready to answer it. Got one super chat. What are the chances the 49ers get Khalil Mack? Well, the Chargers aren't very good. Let's put it that way. So, you know, we'll see who's going to be entering sell mode here over the next few weeks. The chances of getting any one specific player are never high like They're going to probably trade for somebody, right? But I don't know who's going to be available. I don't know who they're going to exactly want and like at a particular position. But Mack has played in a system like Raheem Morris's. I mean, he's played everywhere basically over the course of his career. So, they're going to be looking for pass rushing help, and we will be on the lookout for the 49ers looking for pass rushing help. What's the update on OBJ? The 49ers signed Dante Pettis. They chose Dante Pettis as their veteran receiver. As I talked about yesterday, the 49ers would be looking for a vet to add to the practice squad to help them get through practices and potentially games without screwing up on routes, somebody who knows his way around the league, knows his way around the system. OBJ obviously somebody who might have qualified for that and maybe they'll still need that moving forward, but Dante Pettis definitely qualifies for that since he's actually played for Shanahan with the 49ers before. Do I really think the offense will sink that much without Evans? I think the offense is going to be different without Mike Evans. I think you've got to change like you saw it last week. Without Mike Evans, you cannot run the game plan designed for when you have Mike Evans. That's why they struggled there in that two-drive stretch at the end of the first half after they lost Mike Evans or right around when they did lose Mike Evans. The separation down field wasn't what they were needing it to be and they they just needed to recommit to the run game, recommit to the short passing game and they did. And they still have Christian McCaffrey, they still have George Kittle. It's not just that they've lost Mike Evans and I don't know if they're he's going to be out this week, but they did lose him for for the end of the game in week three. It's that Ricky Pearsall is also out. It's that Demarcus Robinson is also out. It's that De'Sean Shrubling is also out. Then your top four separators are out if if if Mike Evans is out. That changes how you can call games. Now I think that the best game plan against the Denver Broncos might be that paired down game plan that we saw in the second half against the Cardinals anyway given the success that Kansas City had running it. Given the lack of success that the Rams had once they started letting Matthew Stafford do too much with those interceptions. So I think naturally even if you don't have Mike Evans, you move into the second half game plan against Arizona against Denver to try to diffuse that pass rush. And you've got so many good players and such a good quarterback and a good offensive line and a good great play-caller in Kyle Shanahan that that that it should work against the Broncos. But I still think that this because of the fact that the 49ers defense is not playing lights out without Bosa, it's probably the formula for a close game against Denver. I mean, this was a team that was in the AFC Championship, probably would have been in the Super Bowl last year if their quarterback had not gotten hurt. Christian Kirk is not eligible to return until week five. So, that's next week off of injured reserve against Denver. The 49ers could theoretically run more 13 personnel, but I, you know, it it's probably going to be classified as 22 or or 12 because of the fact that Kyle Juszczyk is a fullback, but he's playing a little bit of tight end. Uh I mean, if you're running 13, then it's Kittle, it's Farrell, it's Juszczyk on the field. If push comes to shove, you might have to go to that if you're so low on receivers. But, you know, well, one of the best developments of last week for San Francisco is that we saw Jordan Watkins step up and played a Z at a high level, at a trusted level with Brock Purdy. And that allowed Deebo Samuel to stay in the gadget role and I think that that allows you to continue on with the personnel packages that you've already been showing. All right, I'm headed down to the team facility. Everybody, thanks for watching. Hopefully, you enjoy the uptick in snaps from Malik Mustafa. Welcome back to Malik. We'll see if that increases from 18 to any more this week against the Broncos as the 49ers are getting creative in that secondary. Hopefully, a lot of good information for you guys. If you liked it, hit that subscribe button, hit the like button. Check out my article on the San Francisco Standard. I'll pin it in the comment section and we'll talk to you very soon.

text: No, you saw Ruben kind of running around with trainers and Ya was over there. What's the status of your two outside? >> Yaya, we think will be okay. Whether you're a first round pick or whether you're a free agent, you got to touch the field for the first time at some point. And then you got to play and he's just got to play. >> Have you emphasized how critical this this week's game is to the team? >> It's very critical. How do you get Winfield in a position to make more splash plays, Todd? Or is >> we just got to use him more.
