You know, we had to we had to we had to step our game up. >> What kind of opportunity is that when you have the strange schedule where you're going to be home a bunch? >> You know that I hadn't thought about it until you asked. So, uh, it's great that we're going to be at home, but we we got to we got to play one game at a time, you know, and just stack those games. >> Mike, one player we probably don't ask a lot about is Jaylen Sindell. Just his leadership. He seems just about going about his business. >> Yeah, he's he's he's um a great player. He's a great center, uh, decisive, you know, uh, the way the NFL is going, teams are getting to different looks from different personnels, things like that. So, you got to be able to identify these things and be able to hit targets. The second level, he does all those things. So, um he's playing good football. >> Nick, uh in I know that uh first game he played nine plays. In this game, he played more, but pretty much most of what he did was at the line of scrimmage and and dropping into coverage. Is that part of the plan that increased the play count and then maybe ask him to do more as things go forward? >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, he's a that's he did a lot of things that he did last year. Um, but we'll we'll keep it's a combination of expanding his role and then it's also a combination of where where do we feel like is is best for us and best for him on a week toe basis. So, he's doing a great job. >> I don't think we asked on Monday, but how did Sam come out of the weekend? >> Good. Good. >> I've got one sort of out of left field for you asking because I'm supposed to. Uh, what would you think about the possibility of NFL allowing coaches to challenge pass interference again? Like they I think they did it for one season a few years ago. >> Uh, I need to know more like logistically on how it was going to work because it it didn't work that one year. It just basically went away, you know? I don't think I How many challenges got overturned that year? Like one maybe. >> Yeah, it was not many. So, >> anything else? >> Okay. All right. Thank you.

title: Nick Emmanwori: "The Defense Is Going To Be The Real Deal" | Seattle Seahawks
text: How's it going? >> Going good. How's >> it felt these last couple weeks kind of building up, you know, the time you missed in the training camp, preseason to to kind of have to ramp up in the regular season? >> Uh, it's been feeling good. Uh, everything's going along uh kind of as we expected, you know, kind of weird offseason. So, having the challenge to like ramp up at different times and trying to figure out a good plan, which we've been following, and it's uh been pretty good getting me up to speed. Is it tough to be patient when like you're dressed, you're playing, but they're telling me, "Okay, we're only going to do a little bit this week." >> Yeah, it is to be honest. Uh I mean, you know, I trust the coaches, trust the medical staff and stuff, but you know, as a competitor, I want to go out there and uh play win games and and be on the field. So, it's kind of uh new something new I'm experiencing. >> You went through uh obviously OTAAS and mini camps. Uh at what point did you realize, man, I got to take care of this and and get something done? Uh it was it was it was like a I can't really really explain it. Uh but it was like just a gut feeling just a you know like everything was like kind of feeling good in OTAAS but it was kind of different doctor opinions and stuff trying to figure out what was the best thing to do. So ultimately the thought process was just to go ahead and get it done with over with. So, like I didn't want to be week eight, week nine or something and like it's still bugging me and I can't be out there in the middle of the season which would definitely like you know just make things weird for for the team and everybody. >> I'm guessing you're not even thinking about the injury now. So, I mean how how does that feel just to just play not even think about the injury? >> Yeah, it feels good. Uh super excited to get back out there, you know, uh feel free, feeling fast, miss a lot of time, but I mean I was staying staying uh connected through the mind and through through my teammates. So, it feels good to get back out there and like show show everybody that I I still got it. >> How much was it bothering you as you were like getting ready for training camp? >> Uh, it wasn't bothering me too bad. Like the best way I could explain it was like some days I felt like 100% to go and then some other days I was kind of like on the 75 to 85%. So, like you know like some days I woke up and I you know it was just a weird thing. So, >> was it like limiting you in any way like physically movement wise or was it just like on some days it's going to hurt and it's going to be a problem? I think it was I I want to say it was really limiting me. It was like a little bit of both as far as far as like if I kind of like turned at the wrong like at the wrong time or it was just a weird mechanisms and weird movements would cause it to, you know, flare up or whatever. So, it it was just something that just got to get taken care of. But, you know, some doctors opinions were saying that maybe you didn't need it, maybe you did. So, it was kind of like the 50-50 of whether when or if we should do it. When you were coming out on some of those third downs in Washington, there's there's some school of thought that you learn a lot by watching from the sidelines, but I have a feeling you were probably steamed and want to get on the field. Was there any learning going on on those third downs? >> Yeah. Uh yeah, that was kind of tough, especially like, you know, again, I'm a competitor and I, you know, I want to be out there. I want to kind, you know, always first instinct, you know, to listen to your body, but you got to just follow the medical staff and listen to the coaches and know I mean, no matter what happens, you know, just got to live with it. So definitely frustrated that I really couldn't be out there at all times. So, you know, who knows? So, >> how are you um seeing teams try to attack your defense this year compared to last year? >> You know, it's still early in the season, so like it's kind of hard to tell to get a gauge on like what's everyone what everybody's trying to do. Like, you know, like in the Commander game, they did a lot of totally different stuff on film that we seen that we had to adjust on the fly. So, like I think as the season goes on, even our defense, you know, like you know, we haven't really even ramped up to getting our full packages or like seeing everything we can do, like seen our our defense flourish yet. So, like, you know, everybody's still ramping up and I think in the next couple weeks we'll we'll we'll really see where we start taking our strides as a defense and a team. So, >> all that time that you had uh being sidelined during training camp, like what was what was your biggest priority to maximize that time since you couldn't be out there practicing with the team or doing anything? >> Yeah, honestly, it was uh I was working out a lot and staying sharp mentally. I mean, for me, >> you know, football's kind of like things a lot of things just click for me easily. So, like I wasn't really worried about getting backtracked as far as like the X and O's, but just making sure my body is like up to go. I didn't want to come in any lighter, lose any weight. So, I was really doing a lot of lifting and make sure my body is like built for the season on. So, >> you said it was a weird offseason for you. I'm probably asking the obvious, but what about it was weird? Like what specifically? >> Uh, probably say like after the Super Bowl, uh, you know, knowing I had a little issue with my ankle, probably just trying to figure out what I need to do with that. But, I mean, ramping up from there, it was healing good, feeling good. I was working out with cleats on in the offseason. So, and then coming back for OTAA, still feeling good. So, it was just a lot of stuff I was dealing with as far as like, do I really need it? Do I not need it? Uh, what's it going to be like later on in the fall? Um, still feeling, you know, coming off the Super Bowl high. Um, trying to get back focused for the next season. So, it was just a lot of stuff that, you know, as my first offseason that, you know, rookie, it's kind of hard for me to like grasp like what I was really kind of dealing with. But ultimately, um, everything turned out good. You know, I'm here now healthy, ready to go and, uh, to help the team. So, I mean, all that stuff really doesn't it's in the past now. >> Sorry. Your your recovery from the surgery was one of the story lines that they followed a lot during Hard Knocks. Was that at all strange for you kind of having that be something that was a focus almost every week? >> Uh, not really. Uh, just cuz, you know, I didn't really want to hide it from the world. You know, I'd rather everybody see what I'm going through and, uh, see the process of the whole storyline, how I come back from it, uh, what's going on. So, I didn't want to, you know, keep everybody in the dark or shy away from it, you So, I mean, it is what it is. Like, just got to deal with it. So, it was kind of cool. It was kind of cool that Hard Knight kind of made story lines about it so I can see it and, you know, it's a it's a piece in history. So, >> knowing that you eventually had to get surgery on it now, what going back to the Super Bowl, what what do you kind of reflect on that and playing playing through it a couple days later and what that whole thing was like? >> Yeah, the whole mindset, I mean, I think it was worth it. Uh, but dealing with that through the Super Bowl, like my mindset was just like, I mean, it wouldn't have really felt complete for me to work my way all the way up through the season, all the playoff games, just not to play in the Super Bowl, like you know, last game of the season. Uh, so it was a no-brainer for me to go out there and I think it was worth it. Like, uh, whatever everything that came with it, you know, Super Bowl champion, uh, great season, ended off right. So, I knew I would have slept great if I didn't play in that game. Like, I would have been like, you know, it would have been eaten at me. So, I just had to do it. That type type of dude I am. But, um, it it was worth it. It was great. Um, yeah. >> Whenever you're like all the way back and you're playing as much as everybody planned for, what do you feel like is going to be the biggest difference in your role this season compared to last year? >> Um, I think with the I mean, common sense, you know, we had some departures in the secondary with Kobe and uh, Reek, but I think, you know, stepping up in a bigger role just wherever the coaches find fit. But, you know, even with the departures, I think Mike's done a great job filling in holes or we can't even notice that, you know, things are missing. And, um, you know, whenever I get back and we fully ramp up, uh, I think the defense is going to be it's going to be real. It's going to be real deal. It's going to be even better than last year. So, >> you uh, last year coming out of school, you know, we're we're somewhat well known, but now, you know, after your rookie year, you're pretty well known across the NFL. What what's that been like, that journey for you, like off the field and dealing with that? Uh, it's been it's been it's been amazing. Honestly, it's a blessing. Uh, you know, if you asked me coming out uh coming out the draft or even my a week into my coming to Seattle like what I expected everything to go down, I would have told you exactly everything for me, what what was what was going to happen. So, it feels good um having goals that I set before anything and then completing those goals and having future goals that I'm reaching out for that I can see myself uh completing and getting to. So, I mean, across the NFL world, you know, my name's pretty much known a little bit. They know me as a good defensive player. Uh, but I'm trying to become like one of the def the best defensive players in the league and uh just step myself for that. You know, a lot of things I did miss on that I want to get. anything else? Thank you, sir. >> Yeah. Thank you. Yeah.

title: Wink Martindale: 'Jerry Jones can call me' to help Cowboys, 'buyer beware' on Giants' J.J. McCarthy
text: All right, everybody. It's the episode you're waiting for every week. Now, it is Wednesdays with Wink and it is here in week four. Pat Leonard, New York Daily News NFL columnist and Giants beat writer, but of course the star of the show, veteran NFL defensive coordinator, Wink Martindale back on the show brought to you by Edge Boost here on Talking Ball with Pat Leonard. Wink, how goes it? >> Everything's great. Everything's great. Hey, how about those Giants? first place at in the NFC East, you know what I mean? So, it's it's it's going well. >> No doubt. And it's not only is it going well, but it's going haywire around here with new news and headlines dropping every day as John Harbaugh is trying to turn over this roster and get the Giants going. Wink. And the big one that dropped this week, of course, the acquisition, the trade for JJ McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings. Third string quarterback. The Giants send a fifthround pick. of course won a national championship at Michigan and I believe Wink when you were coming on with the Wolverines that was the spring that he was entering and going into the draft. >> Yeah. >> What what do you think uh what do you what do you know about JJ and what do you think about this move for the Giants in this fit? >> Well, I mean I I think that first of all is you know the the war of attrition through the NFL season. You're starting to see it and we're seeing it early. uh you know with all the different injuries of all the different teams and um you know I I I think it's one of those things that just can't get blown out of proportion. Um you know I know that you know everybody's excited just because it's a new name you know added to that the quarterback room but you know let's let's see it for what it is. you know, he's, you know, Kevin Okonnell was, you know, is a quarterback whisperer as as people have said and, you know, has done a nice job offensively and he was their third team quarterback. Uh, to me, it's a little bit of buyer beware, you know what I mean? If he's the third team quarterback in Minnesota, uh, they took him with what, the 10th pick, I believe. and um you know they're they're they're they're moving on from him you know really fast for you know a fifth round pick but you know I I think it's you know like I said buyer beware let's just see where it's at. I don't think it changes anything you know for this weekend. Uh and I think John even alluded to that that James is the starter in the near future. And you know, I understand, you know, the excitement of the fantasy football owners and and even the Giants fans because it's it's it's like, hey, look, we're trying. And um you know, I think it does bolster the quarterback room from what you know, who else they had who all they had in there. But um I think it's a a ways away to see, you know, where he's at. >> Is it a is this an interesting or a challenge now for Harbaugh to of course, like you said, he brings another player into the quarterback room. It's it has more players in it and more talent in it than it did two days ago. But is it a challenge too now to balance the team's buy in as you acclimate McCarthy? Because in other words, Jamus is the starter now, which Harbaugh said, but now you have this young guy who could conceivably challenge Jamus for the starting job soon. And he also has this mobile skill set. John gets information from his brother, so he has that kind of recommendation and that behind him, you know, even going into next year with Jackson Dark coming back into the fold. It just seems like a delicate situation that you're creating by bringing him in. But how would you see it as as a as an NFL coach and knowing how John Harbaugh handles these types of situations? >> Yeah. And and you know, let me clarify again. I'm not there. I haven't talked to John. you know, um, you know, his brother has enough problems or rather, you know, to see if JJ McCarthy can get on his roster. You know, I'm sure he had a lot of good things. They won a national championship together. Uh, but, you know, I'm sure that, you know, it's it's it's one of those things that, you know, we we'll see here in the next five years. Is he going to be a Troy Smith, you know, like Ohio State's Heisman Trophy winner, or is he going to be an NFL quarterback? Uh, I think he still has a long way to go. I think that uh you know what I saw on tapeuh from his Minnesota play was you know it was it was hard for him to see things and his foot footwork you know showed that you know like he was almost panicking sometimes and and there you know he he he does have a you know he does have an arm >> but it's like erratic you know from what I saw you know >> it I I'm just saying let's be patient. patient. This isn't a This isn't a a fixall great trade. This is a band-aid on a room that, you know, needs another quarterback. I do, you know, agree with you what you said about his mobility. Um, he, you know, he he might be able to, you know, move into the offense and, you know, do some good things, but I I'm I'm not ready to give my this the stamp of, you know, approval. You just got to wait and see it. not totally fair and balanced analysis. And and I think the one thing I heard Harbaugh say during his press conference when we were asking him about the trade that rang true to me is John doesn't want to hear about anything other than beating the Cardinals. And like I know that's I know that that is cliche, but that really does seem to be the where he's at. >> No, it's not cliche. It's the NFL. You got to win this week and and he's concentrating on Arizona. um things will work out the way they're supposed to work out, you know, like you know, they you know, he probably be a scout team quarterback this week and you know, see, you know, see how he's throwing the ball and how he's moving and, you know, and all those different things. Um but, you know, Jameus is the starting quarterback. That's what John said. So, you know, that's that's what they're going to take into Arizona. And so pivoting in the short term, Wink, as we stay on the Giants, you know, if JJ whether he's the number two or whether he's the number three scout team inactive emergency QB, the guy's on the field, right? They're going to decide whether the Giants improve to three and one when they take on the Cardinals. And this week, as we promised to the fans, and by the way fans, stop right now, subscribe if you haven't already. Smash that like button for Wink. We need to get to 12,500 subscribers, not only to grow the channel, but so we can get Wink convince him to go live with us and with you together. So the first Wink live episode that's going to drop, that's going to happen when we get those subscriber numbers up. So don't forget to hit that subscribe button now. See, Winka, you didn't have to jump in. I I remember. >> Thank you. And And it's like, come on. What What are we doing? I thought we were Giants fans. >> [laughter] >> Yeah. Yeah. Where are the Giants fans? >> There's a lot more Giants fans than 7500. >> And we're and we're giving some love and we're giving love around the league, too. So, it's Giants fans, but it's we're giving love around the league here. >> All right. So, I mentioned the fans because I did solicit some questions this week. >> Okay. >> From our Giants fans on Talking Ball postgame live after the Giants bar and burner 12 to7 win over the Titans out there. >> Win's a win. A win is a win. >> Win is a win. And uh Joe says, "What is wrong, Wink, with the pass rush? Are Kavon and Abdul Carter still players that as top 10 draft picks with no return so far can still play good ball?" So Joe wants to know, "Wink, especially with Brian Burns out for the year now with the torn ACL, one sack in three games, what is wrong with the pass rush? What do the Giants need to be able to do on defense to get to the quarterback better in your opinion? Well, I I think that, you know, it it's a team, you know, and you you've probably seen the sign there in the building, the team, the team, the team, you know, and right now the way teams are playing, and I think John alluded to this in his last press conference, the way teams are playing to them is they have the full playbook because right now the offense isn't threatening >> their defense. Does that make sense? So they have their whole playbook. Uh so teams are you know trying to run the ball. Um and you know play action pass which is the best pass in the NFL statistically you know through Gen stats and everything else all the other stats and analytics that go with it. Um it's it's in a tough spot but you know to me as a coordinator this is just me so it doesn't make it absolutely 100% right. To me as a coordinator, I think you have to attack on first and second down, you know, with pressures. Um, and it's not just on those two edge guys, you know, I mean, you have to you see their protections and no one to, you know, to to attack an offense. So, they just can't sit there and call whatever they want to call like it's a four-minute drill, if you will, you know. And um then you know off you know offensively they need to score points so they can get that pass rush cranked up. You know we always looked you know we were always jacked whenever you got a two-score lead because that's when it was time to go hunting you know as with your pass rushers and you know it hasn't been that yet and it's still way early in the season. Um, you know, I I understand the the frustration that, you know, that you're not seeing Abdul Carter, you know, burn an edge and go sacking quarterback, but, you know, right now they're hunkering down to stop the run and then they have to convert from, you know, the the run to the play action pass, and that that's that's hard for anybody to do. And, you know, he's, you know, I I think he's improving just watching him on tape. Uh, and it's, you know, the same thing with Kavon his first year. And I know it's not his first year, but it, you know, the next year he had 11 and a half sacks because you got to work at that. You got to get him in some one-on-one situations. Um, you know, they're going to say chips and everything else. Well, you got to run some, you know, some pass rush stunts and but you have to get a lead before you start critiquing your pass rush. That that's that's just my opinion. >> And, you know, to me, that's that's a team thing. That's not just a a defensive thing. >> That makes sense. When you talk about Giants needing to be more aggressive on defense on first and second down to get the teams into those third and longs, are you sending just hypothetically, and I know it probably depends who you're playing and what you know their tendencies are, >> but are you sending a run blitz on a first down or are you making calls for pressures where you're expecting, let's say, a pass or a play action pass? Are you sending pressures where you know whether it is run or pass on that first down >> that you think there's some tendency that you can take care of? Like how how do you balance the aggressiveness on first down >> uh let's say bringing a pressure with not trying to you know guess wrong. I >> think that you know it depends on your opponent who you're playing you know game plan wise of when you want to attack and how you want to attack it. Um, you know, I I I think that, you know, your run pressures can fit with your, you know, a lot of run pressures hit when they do do play action pass. >> So, um, you know, it's it's one of those things that you have to sit down as a staff and say, how are we going to attack this game again? You know, do we need to get them behind the sticks? Um, you know, and I'm not sure that Arizona is that type of game. You know, it's just one of those things you have to to wait and see. But I also know that, you know, the McVey style offense, which Mike runs there in Arizona, um they don't they don't like pressures. They don't like, you know, making them, you know, you know, choose when you have your your mic, your your your dime and your nickel up on the line of scrimmage or your safety down on the line of scrimmage of figuring out who they need to block. So, >> you know, I it's it's one of those things. You'll know that they can't handle your pressures when you start seeing bubble screens and terror screens and, you know, the the RPO stuff and you it's just a constant mix and it's a feel for the coordinator. So when you say they don't like it, are you alluding to basically they instead of changing their personnel to address it, they'd rather just call a different play to alleviate it, but they don't they don't want to be they don't want to be out of let's say like their 11 personnel, >> right? And then you got to check when they check and you know it becomes a chess match and that's the fun part about calling defense and calling offense in the National Football League. >> Very insightful, always interesting. Um, Wink, one more Giants question and then we'll branch out to to the league. And this is just happening as we're as we're talking. I mean, that right now, I alluded to it right off the bat. I mean, we literally don't have like a single day right now with some sort of significant Giants news. It's like the the the ground is shifting beneath our feet. Odell Beckham Jr. ma made the team out of camp. Calvin Austin tore his knee and uh Beckham makes the team. Sllayton makes the team. Harbaugh cuts Sllayton and it looks like with neighbors coming back slowly that Beckham might get a lot of chance to play, but Seldom plays in the first three weeks. What do you think of cutting Odell, you know, getting rid of a fan favorite like that? Uh maybe his usage or lack thereof. Um, and and correct me if I'm saying anything wrong with this, but you know, when I worked for Mr. Davis uh with the Raiders, he always, you know, would say things just give you gems, little gems on, you know, watching especially older guys cuz he no one loved an older player than Mr. Davis. I mean, my first year there, we had Tim Brown and Jerry Rice there at the end of their career and they couldn't run anymore. >> And, you know, I I haven't been to practice. I don't know, you know, if if there's some unusual drops, you know, when you when a receivers's catching a ball, I'm talking about seven on seven and, you know, in practice and things like that. That was the first red flag of he might be losing his legs and it's hard to come back after a year off at that age. It really is, especially at wide receiver. So, I don't, you know, I don't know if they did it. I don't know if Odell wanted to, you know, look for another team. You know, that that could be as you know, true as well. I don't know. Um but um you know, I know he'll always have that catch that he had there in Metife Stadium and uh like I said, he's he's had a great career and you know, he's won a Super Bowl and um you know, I I you know, I just hope the best for him and you know, that he stays healthy and you know, if he wants to go get on another team, I hope he can do that. Fascinating how much change is happening here in New York. But we knew it was coming because John Harbaugh was brought here to clean it up. Five years, 100 million. They have a chance to win this Sunday. Uh Arizona's a good football team. >> I mean that that that NFC West is brutal, but they're a good football team and they got a good running back and they got a functional quarterback. Um, so it it's uh, you know, it's going to be a great challenge for him. You know, it's going to be a bigger challenge than what it was last week against the Titans. Uh, I mean, it really is. I get it. >> I I I laughed because you said it's going to be a bigger challenge than the Titans and I'm just thinking, well, I mean, that that doesn't take much. I mean, holy cow. it. I'm just, you know, just you you your eyes don't lie to you when you're watching it. >> You know, >> one first Yeah. one first down on six possessions, five five punts and a missed field goal with one first down in the first half. Titans on the Giants >> Yeah. Now, you know, I'm sure that John wanted to get a bigger lead and expand on the lead and, you know, all those different things where you could actually see your pass rush. Um, but you know, in tight games like that, they're they're playing it close to the vest. they were trying to protect their their rookie quarterback. Um, so, you know, it's and you know, it's it's it's one of those things that to be two in one in the league is a pretty good thing right now. You know, >> no doubt. >> Like I said, you know, speaking of Harballs, you think Jim Jim would like to be two and one right now? >> No doubt. No doubt. >> You know what I mean? So, >> and you speak too to like, you know, the difference in like Jim and John for example. It's like the NFL is so optics driven, but it's also the reality like the expectations for your team coming in matters, right? title: Jeffery Simmons & Amani Hooker on Facing Derrick Henry | Titans Locker Room
text: He's on the other side now, man.  Our job is to go out there and win the running game, and we'll let him start the game.  I mean, for 5 years in a row I've heard Mike Vrabel talk about them getting to step four, step five .  And good things happen.  So our job on offense, one of our key ones this week, is to make him stop his feet, make him stutter in the backfield.  And honestly, what I say every week is this game is won on offense;  and the way we, the way we go, especially this weekend, is the way this team will go .  If we break the skirmish line, good things will happen.  We have to make it jump, stutter, move east and west.  If he goes down , bad things will happen to the defense, which we all know.  So our task in attack is to be truly destructive. Will it be weird to play against him? Absolutely not.  I mean, like I said, he wasn't here. Of course, it's my first time playing against him, but damn. This also applies to me on game day, I don't care who it is. You are on the other side of the line of scrimmage.  I have a family to feed, and a lot of my teammates have families to feed as well.  So, I do everything I can to help them feed their families.  So, unless you're in the two-tone blue and that new Titans uniform, it doesn't really matter.  So, do you see any conversations, and do you guys imagine having a little laugh? Um, I mean, there weren't a few jokes with him at practice when he was here, but I mean, I'm going to talk anyway.  I don't care who it is. I mean, I'm a competitor, man.  I'm sure he had that game under control, but for us, it's that if we could do what we needed to do and do it at our level for four quarters, then none of that would really matter.  I mean, we know who's on the other side of the line of scrimmage.  Um, not just him, but Will Lewis too, so we need to play our football. Jeff, you were a rookie when he carried this franchise. Now your job is to run the franchise.  Is there anything you take with you when you look back on 2019? You know how he did it as a leader and pointed everyone in the right direction.  Everyone has their own different ways of leading.  Um, I mean , I don't remember Derrick talking as much as actually how he trained, how he took care of his body and how he showed younger players like Tajae, and Tajae came in, and other running backs that were under Derrick, how he, I think, led.  Um, it wasn't so much about the conversations.  Um, but the guys that I always shout out when I think of them, like guys like Jurrell Casey, who I had a bigger connection with because he was in our room.  Like I said, my way of leading is that I'm a vocal guy, but I can also go out there and show you what I can do.  So I can't go back and say that I learned so much from him in my debut year .  As I said, it wasn't that big, first of all, it wasn't in my room.  And secondly, you know, I'm also a vocal leader, so... But everyone knows, I guess, going back to what I said earlier, everyone knew about Derrick Henry.  Everyone knew his impact not only on the people in this building but also outside of it, so... Jeff, you guys just lost in the fourth quarter the last two games. How important is it for you guys to keep the defense strong early on Sunday? I won't even take just defense.  I mean, it's always important to start fast, and I think our team needs to start faster.  Um, at all stages, so as not to struggle so much in the fourth quarter sometimes.  You know, these games , yeah, are they won in the fourth quarter?  Many of these games will be won in the fourth quarter.  But if we can start faster and play the way we play in the second half, when you turn on that tape and see Titans football in the second half, you think, 'This is a different team than the one we saw in the first quarter.'  So, um, um, in every game we've ever played, so how can we start faster as a team?  Um, and just finish stronger.  Because we've been basically, especially in the last 2 weeks, um, you know, from the Eagles game to the um, um, the Giants game last week, is that second half of Titans football really good.  How can we achieve this in the first, second, and first and second quarters? Yes, I've heard of him. Um, he's taken us to the playoffs a few times, but, um, yeah, I'm excited to play against him. You know, I've been able to watch him play for another team for a few years now, and, hm, that's going to be exciting.  It will be fun.    Do you think it will be strange to play against him? Hmm, I think so.  I think it will be strange at first.  Hmm, never been on the side of grabbing him, but hearing, you know, what we need for him to win, to be successful, and talking to other guys in the league about what it takes to grab him, hmm, I think we'll be ready. Jeff...Jeff basically said, look, it's pretty simple, just rally, you know, get all 11 goals up to the ball, knock it down and shoot. Yeah, I mean, you don't want it to roll down, do you?  Hmm, he's harder to beat.  If you can make him stop a few times, you will slow him down. He meant so much to this organization. How much do you appreciate how iconic he was when he was here? Yeah, I mean I definitely appreciate it.  I mean, every time I see him, you know, we're great, we're good friends.  Um, you know, he took us, as I said, to the playoffs.  We won games here.  He was a leader. Um, and I respect him a lot.  Did you take anything from him in terms of leadership while he was here and now that you're in this role? Just his professionalism, you know, his daily coming to work and working, whether it's on his skills or on how he works .  He takes lifting weights seriously.  Um, that's something I've picked up on as well, and you know, overall he's just a great guy, a great teammate. Did you feel like you had a pickaxe in your hand last week, and I wonder what it's like to watch this tape afterwards? Yes.  Um, yeah, I thought I had it , but, you know, everything was wet.  I mean , it was wet.  I tried to squeeze her as hard as I could, but, uh, it's Amani, you mentioned the hands.  Uh, when Derrick Henry runs in the secondary, you know, it leads to a lot of memes.  Uh, what's your train of thought if you find yourself facing him between him and the end zone? Yeah, um, I mean , he's going to strike. So it's kind of like boxing, you know?  It's an attempt to wait for him to strike and then make your strike or get to him before he can strike.  So, I mean, he's doing a great job of it.  He is perfecting it.  Um, so our job is just to find ways to bring him down. You've had some good success against Lamar over the years since you've been here. I know it's under a different coaching staff, but can you carry some of those elements over to Sunday?  So, some of the things... Yeah, some of the things that we emphasized a couple of years ago playing...we kind of brought up today with the team staff. But, I mean, he's a great quarterback, the greatest quarterback of all time.  He can use his legs , you know, you don't keep him in the pocket as much as you can, which is hard to do.  Um, and if he's scrambling, don't jump, don't take your feet off. Just act as if you are picking up the ball for the receiver. Yes.  Everyone... Honestly, I mean, you know, I love both of these guys. They show up every day in a great mood.  Um, Coach Crum prepares everyone from the psychological side in meetings, you know, who he asks questions to, whether it's the starter or someone else or, you know, our practice reps, to the distribution of the game where, you know, it's not just the starters doing every rep.  The other guys are also training.  So when you get into that situation, you know, the guy is ready.  He is ready to play.  Um, Coach Crum is very standards-oriented, and the expectations are the same.  Um, you know, losing a guy like that, um, it definitely feels that way, especially um, Slater, when, you know, I felt like he was playing really well, and then after the game you get hit with the news of what happened.  Um, so , it's just the mentality of the next player, and I mean, we all prepared, um, like we were the starting players. So, um, we expect the game to live up to the standards we set for ourselves. When you guys found such a good rhythm together as a five-man attack, do you feel like the next person who comes in as a substitute will just be able to relate to you easily, given how you just mentioned your training? Um, yes, I mean exactly.  I think one thing that's really special about our group is that we have really good chemistry outside of football.  You know, we all communicate.  We all, you know, get along really well together. And then, I think the most important thing is that while we each have our own interests, we all broaden our interests, you know, for example, for me, because I'm into watches, you know, so I talk to Slater about watches and things like that.  From the outside, it may seem like this is not what we do. You know, we spent about two hours together in the afternoon just looking at watches in the store; you know, I mean, we all do these things, and we just look forward to being around each other as a group. You know, whether it's good, bad, or indifferent, we all work hard with the same mindset. We all show up ready to work. Yes, it's definitely hard to lose these guys. I think Jackson did a great job of finishing the game the way he did. And we'll start this week.  The best thing about it is that all of us, Karm Karm, teach and train in such a way that everyone learns and everyone is on the same wavelength.  Um, yes, we will attack this week and we will prepare.  It's just like any other week.  We focus on your game. What works so well for you in terms of pass blocking?  Do you think this is the beginning... Yeah, I think, just trusting our technique, um, getting familiar with the images over the course of the week that we'll get.  Um, yeah, and just getting out there and executing. And you have someone like Kyler who likes to keep the game alive.  Is that what was key for you guys, and is that the biggest adjustment for you over the first few games so far? Yeah, I think when you have a quarterback who likes to keep the plays going, that's great. First, because he can force players to miss in the pocket.  And secondly, it's really, really important to approach this so that the giveaway never ends.  You just have to block until the whistle blows, and that goes for every play. When you guys, you know, were betting on the fourth quarter the last two games, how important is it that you get the game started quickly on offense ? This is extremely important.  A quick start is definitely the key this week.  We start everything we do quickly, and that's how we'll attack throughout the week.    The Ravens defense stands out, what challenges do they pose for you this week?  They have many different images.  They do a lot of good things. They have good players, a lot of pressure, a lot of movement on early attempts, they often use the 14- point mode.  It will be a test, but I think we will have a good workout during the week.

title: Robert Saleh on Cam Ward's Footwork, JC Latham & the Lamar Jackson Challenge | Press Conference
text: Good morning, guys .  So, a very brief injury report.  JFM has back problems. He won't be training today. There are no particular concerns about Sunday.  And Tony and Taj will be absent today too .  Again , I'm not too worried about Sunday.    Do Hernandez and Jackson need surgery? Yes, they will have surgery. Hopefully they will return later this year. What does this mean for the warehouse?  Who do I think will compete for their positions? This is an open question. I'll keep it to myself for now, with all due respect, guys.  But all possible options are being considered . If a scenario arose in which Kuangjo would take the field, where would he rather play: at guard or center?  Even about this. I will refrain from answering.  Thank you. Although I appreciate your question, Paul. What is the impact?  What do you see in Cam's footwork and how does it relate to accuracy? You know, the kind you see at the beginning of games, at least, and it appears more and more often towards the end of matches.  You can see that he feels comfortable in the "pocket". You see he trusts the offensive line. And then, later in the game , you see him kind of fall back into some old habits. But I really think he's getting better at that .  I think he's starting to really appreciate the offensive line because they're protecting him so well , and he's building that trust.  You have to remember how many times he was " grounded" last year.  So I'm sure there 's some kind of post-traumatic stress disorder there.  But he is getting better.  He begins to trust. His footwork becomes more effective throughout most of the game, if you know what I mean. But yes, in terms of accuracy and decision-making, everything for a quarterback starts with footwork. So how do you, as a coaching staff, when these footwork and technique issues continue to arise, hold him accountable and ensure it doesn't happen again? You are watching videos.  You practice this in exercises.  You step out onto the training field. He knows what he needs to do.  He himself feels it when it happens.  And you try to fix it during the game, but like I said, he's fully aware of it and shows he's getting better.  If you watch all three games, you'll see that his footwork, pocket sense, and field awareness improve with every minute of play. I think eventually we'll get to the point where he won't even think about it and we'll all stop talking about it, but he's working non-stop. I know Dabol and his staff are working tirelessly with him to show where he can get better and where he is already showing good results, and we will just continue to improve. But if technique deteriorates as the game progresses, why are there such problems with slow starts to matches this season? Yes, for many reasons.  I mean, in the last game, we lost the ball on the kickoff, dropped a few passes on third down, got a bad call from the referee—it all adds up in the first half.  And the previous week, we couldn't stop the opponent on defense, and I couldn't provide the offense with enough balls for them to make long drives.  So it's a little bit of everything .  It's not always their fault. But this is definitely something we need to get better at. If the slow starts in the first half continue, what will you change in your approach? That's a good question, dude.  We are quite satisfied with our approach.  I think the guys are taking to the field with great enthusiasm and energy. You know, like I said, we...Regarding the last game—we first shot, and if you look at it, it's a change of initiative for about 5 minutes. Otherwise, the advantage in time of possession is not as drastic as people probably think.  They actually gained additional possession.  And from an attacking perspective, it's dropped passes and certain moments that don't quite add up due to lack of communication and execution, but I think we'll fix that.  This is a young team.  We are getting better every day, and if we can maintain the level we showed in the second half of the game, I think we have a chance to become quite strong. You mentioned that Cam values ​​protection.  There was one moment in New York where the defense was very solid, and he seemed to understand that because he almost completely stopped with the ball.    It almost seemed like the game was stopped by a whistle.  And he made an accurate pass.  What did you think when you saw this on the recording ? Um, I wish he would —and we talked about it .  I would like him to use his legs, continue the play and try to find a chance for an explosive attack.  Um, you know, I think that's his trump card.    I think that's where he shines and it was an opportunity, but I also think the defense was so good that it probably surprised him.  It was an incredible defense, but in that situation we talked about it.  You would like him to use his legs to create a sharp moment.    Are you satisfied with such frivolity?  I mean, is it some kind of... No, I mean, he has his own style, but, um, yeah.  As long as he's careful with the ball, it does n't matter. I know you've been praising the offensive line, regardless of who starts .  How confident are you that this group will continue to progress? I'm optimistic because I think Slot does a good job of communicating and helping players get where they need to be.  I think JC right is having a Pro Bowl-level season after three games.  He plays at an outstanding level. And so when someone comes in between the two of them, who I think plays good football, it's beneficial. As for William, were you disappointed by this week's pass-rush against Lamar and his footwork? Um, man, that's four guys against six zones and an elite runner.  He is elite in finding open corridors and ways to break out and create off-the-chart moments, but countering him is always a challenge.  We are confident in the speed of our defensive line and hopefully our cover will work and we can catch up with them. Last season, Cam led the league in 20+ yard passing efficiency. He attempted six of these this season, but failed to complete any.  So , you mentioned that the offensive line defends well, you have players you believe in.  Is this, shall we say, a feature or a mistake in your attack system?  Do you hope he'll reveal this part of the game later, or are you trying to keep it a secret? No, this is probably the evolution of defense in general.  I think the Jets play a lot with two safeties in the deep zone.  Just like the Eagles. The weather last week was not conducive to long-distance transmissions. But you try to find a balance between what provides protection and what you are capable of at that moment.  From a long-range shooting perspective, you can't just line up and throw the ball down the field if everyone is covered.    You have to be selective and remain a disciplined quarterback: if the defense doesn't allow for risk, choose the best available option. But there will be moments, and if you want to open up the backs and force them to drop the safeties, you have to be able to play the takeaway. I think we did it in the second half.  We started playing well off the line, and they started dropping the safeties closer to the line, which created a few opportunities for our receivers on the wings.  So it's all interconnected, everything works together.  Yes, I would have happily kicked the ball down the field and played old-fashioned Raiders football, throwing it in all directions, but the league has changed so much that they force you to take what they give you. So you're saying they're playing against him differently, significantly differently , than they did last season when he was able to do that? I don't know if that's true, I wo n't comment on that.  I won't talk about last year, but I know that the trend in defense right now is to provoke you into taking the ball with two deep safeties.  And if you can't, you're in for a very, very long day. How much do you think Daboll and Cam agreed on understanding the concept, what needed to be done, and even the weekly changes? Honestly, I think they do a great job of communicating.  I really enjoy listening to their dialogue. I like listening to them talk.  The right questions are being asked on both sides Correct answers are provided .  And you understand, we are implementing a new system, and I think everyone is still trying to get to know each other better. Um, I wish it would go faster like everyone else, but there's no doubt that the process is going well. The work is going well.  We saw a glimpse of that in the second half of last week when we had three very long drives, looked efficient, made explosive plays and got to the 10-yard line three times.  So, it's only a matter of time before things start to work out.    The reason I asked is because last Wednesday he expressed how much he likes hard play action and playing under center.  And if you look at Sunday's game against the Eagles, it worked well.  There were those elements on Sunday, but there were significantly fewer of them in the game against the Giants .  So I wonder why there wasn't more of that hard play-action and play under center. Um, yeah, no, those elements will always be there, but I'll put it this way: defense and what you're trying to do with the game plan will always dictate what you want to achieve.  And, you know, I know we had a few situations where, talking about last week, there were a lot of options for Cam , a lot of choices between running and passing depending on the situation.    For example, after leaving the locker room: they gave us a "two-shell" defense, we beat them 8 yards, gave it again—we beat them again.  They lowered the safety, we got our bearings and launched an explosive attack on Cornell from the left flank.  So, it's just what you need to do at a specific moment to attack the defense depending on their actions against you. When do you want your offense to dictate more of its defense terms, rather than the other way around? I think that in itself dictates the situation, for example if the defense offers you one thing and you have a set of tools you want to attack them with.  So I believe that the attack always dictates the terms. From a defensive perspective, I like to think we dictate, but in reality we are just reacting to the offense. But you have to, you have to be able to adapt depending on what you see. If you know you're going to hit a wall, you want the quarterback to have options, and I think that's something we're growing into, something Cam is getting used to, and something I know we're going to get better at. Derrick Henry had a special aura here, from his performance to the way he interacted with people.  When a team has such a unique player and then he leaves, there is a certain void created.  I know, I know you weren't here , but you saw what he was doing and you probably felt it. How difficult is it to somehow fill this gap, if it is perhaps impossible for one person to do it ?    Do you mean mending a broken relationship? No, I mean replace. Oh, replace a guy like Derrick?    In all the ways he dragged the organization down. First of all, I still think he has this aura.  This guy is an incredible football player who is headed to the Hall of Fame. Everything you hear about him: his work habits off the field, the way he interacts with people, and who he is on the field.  I mean, he was a very special person in that regard.  I never coached him, but I always had the opportunity to see him from afar and play against him.  And again , he's a beast, still running like he's 25 years old.  So it's a huge challenge, and yeah, anytime to replace a Hall of Fame player, it's not going to be easy. Last question, T- D. I'm sure as a defensive coach you're biased, but what are your thoughts on a possible review of referee decisions? Hmm, I don't like that.  So I think that as frustrating as it is, the human factor of refereeing is still part of the game.  I think that's what makes the game special—human error.  It's like baseball.  Every judge has their own style. You know, he can serve high, he can serve high and close to the zone.  Or it can be served low. Whatever that strike zone is, that's what makes baseball special.  This is not a fixed strike zone.  So I think judges make mistakes.  This is very annoying.  People are losing their jobs because of this.  But that's what great.

title: LIVE: HC Dan Quinn Speaks To The Media Before The First Practice In London | Washington Commanders
text: What's up? >> Good morning, afternoon. >> It's good to see you guys. Uh this is my first game as a coach in England and uh man, I'm pumped to be here. It's cool here at the Grove. This is our headquarters for a week. It's absolutely a fantastic setup. people people often ask uh me or the team like what's different about you know international games and you say travel or customs or the venue but the thing I've wanted to emphasize with the team the most is what's exactly the same and those are our anchors of what a Wednesday a Thursday and a Friday look like in terms of our preparation to get ready and so that's a lot of the reason for coming early so we can get back into that process uh the quicker we get to that less focus on what's different and more focused on what's the same. So, we're pumped. We're ready to get rolling with practice today and um open it up for you guys. >> John, I was going to ask about your approach to the week. What went into that to come over at this time and also right at that just how did you come up? >> Yeah, fortunately we also have like an excellent performance team. Jeff Kaplan, Dr. Forest, Nick Frell, nutritionist. title: Wayne Gretzky Breaks Down The Top Storylines You Should Know Heading Into This NHL Season
text: Ladies and gentlemen, the man who is known as the greatest hockey player of all time for good reason. I from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania used to say he was the second best player or maybe third best player in the history of hockey. Then some people as I continued to say this publicly came up to me and said, "Hey, do you know if you got rid of just goals entirely, this guy would still lead the history of the NHL in points." So, not just like good at scoring, also good at setting up and manipulation of uh defense and also was willing to hit and also lad of the lads. This is by far the great one. No questions asked. Now he's on TV with TNT talking about the greatness of hockey. Ladies and gentlemen, Wayne Gretzky. >> Nice to see everyone. Thanks for having me on. And you're right. Last night was a great start. Uh the game couldn't be in better shape and it's fun to watch. I'm a fan and I love it. It's And you know tonight Pittsburgh and Philly Pittsburgh's got some things to prove after getting beat last year upset in the playoffs by the Young Flyers. So Sid is on top of his game. I look to him for him to have another great season. He's defying age. He gets better every year. >> How many years did you play in uh the NHL? How old were you whenever you hung up the skates? Finally, >> I turned pro at 17. One year in the WHA, uh, in Indianapolis, and then Edmonton, of course, >> and then 19 years. So, I got 20 years of professional hockey. Um, and you know, the the great thing about the game was playing the games. And one of the reasons I retired was the older you get, the more you have to train. And I just mentally couldn't figure out, okay, how am I going to train two to three hours a day, five or six days a week, and that's when I knew it was time to retire. Well, the game certainly misses you and the game is happy that you're back calling it. Sydney Crosby, I believe in his 22nd season now all with Pittsburgh. We're incredibly lucky and thankful that he's there alongside Gino and Tanganger. That's at 7:30 tonight. Also, Islanders, Maple Leafs, and Kings and Avalanche. Let's go back to yesterday a little bit with you talking about the games. Carolina Hurricanes now start their trek after being world champions for the first time. Florida Panthers debut a brand new team with Brady Kachchuck out there. They had to watch the entire Stanley Cup banner celebration before the game even started. Thought it was a lock for the Panthers. What do you expect from those two teams, both the Carolina Panthers and or Carolina Hurricanes and a Florida Panthers? >> Well, listen, I don't think there's anything worse than being a Stanley Cup champion or Super Bowl champion and then losing and then the next year you go in and you have to see your biggest rival raising the banner. I I think that you're standing on the blue line gritting your teeth thinking and hoping, okay, I can't wait to get this game started and try to win back what we had two years ago. So, you know, Florida, that Bill Zito's done an incredible job putting together a really good young hockey club. And last year was not really a reflection of their team. They had a lot of key injuries for a lot of the year. Matthew Tuchuk is such a big part of the success of that team. you know, he's such an agitator, but it's one thing to be an agitator, but you got to be able to play the game. It's It doesn't do the team any good if you're just an agitator. But Matthew's a leader. He scores big goals. He makes big plays. The two guys that I kind of relate to when I played were Theo Flurry was that kind of a player and Shawn Avery. Those two guys, they were agitators, but they could play the game. And you got to be able to do that. And so now adding Brady, the brother, and you know, you can see it how close they are as a family. Their father's a Hall of Famer. They got two Olympic gold medals. They got two Stanley Cups now. Um, >> it's a good time for that family to go buy a lottery ticket. >> Yeah, I think they already I think they've already hit it a couple times now. >> Obviously, it's earned and deserved. I'm excited for Florida Panther to get back into the conversation of Stanley Cup alongside obviously the Pittsburgh Penguins. AJ has a question for you. Great one. >> Yeah. I'm just curious. Yourself as a player, when you were playing, would you attack certain goalies? Like would you have a book on each goalie? I think like as football players, we think, hey, you you're going to play against like certain defensive coordinators and their calls and what they're doing. I'm thinking for you scoring so many goals and points obviously. Do you have a specific plan for each goalie as you go? >> Yeah. You know, and I think that the one thing that I learned about playing professional sports is I had so much respect for our coaching staff and I was like a sponge and Mark Messier was the same way and Paul Coffee was that way. We wanted all the intel that we could get and you know the game is played at such a high pace and it's so fast and it's way faster today than it was back when we played. But there's always idiosyncrasies that goalies have whether he catches right-handed, catches left-handed, if he likes to go down, if he opens his legs, uh if he comes out and challenges you a little bit more than another guy. So yeah, all that information is vital because the game is so fast. >> Yeah, the it feels like modern technology as well. We have stats and analytics on everything. I think goalies probably even have stats and analytics on where guys like to shoot, you know, but how much information >> Oh, absolutely. And the better the goalie, the more that that they take in and the more video that they watch. It's like every other sport, the best athletes and the the the most unique players on those teams, those are hardest working guys usually. And take Sydney Crosby and Ovetchkin. I mean, they're 20 years in and both of them are still important and imperative to the success of their team. Um, and that's a good thing. And and the other side of it is we got some great young players now with Celibbrini and McDavid and McKinnon. um on and on. It's just bard in Chicago. It's just a great time for the National Hockey League and these kids are really good athletes. >> Ticket sales up last night for the start of the NHL season across the board and all the arenas. Hopefully that will continue because the sport is incredible and awesome. You just mentioned one name there and you talk about the next generation. A lot of pressure. Go ahead, Debbie. >> Yeah, he's talking about Conor McDavid and if you're a casual outside of hockey, you know, everyone says he's the greatest player of his generation, but you also, hey, when is he going to win? Well, how much pressure is on him now as he approaches kind of that 30-y old mark? >> Yeah, I'm sure there's a little bit more pressure right now than there was say five, six, seven years ago. You know, there's no question he's the best player of the game. Um the question might be in a couple years, is he go down as the greatest player ever lived? Uh I always tell people that Bobby or and Gordy How are the two greatest players ever lived? Mark Messi was the best player ever played uh played with and Mario Lemieux was the greatest player ever played against. So, you know, corner there's always a stigma about winning a Stanley Cup and I know him really well. Nobody wants to win a championship worse than he does. So, hopefully his time will come. I know it's not from a lack of effort or dedication or love of the sport. And I hope one day he gets that opportunity to lift the Stanley Cup. He he definitely deserves it. He's the one guy team sell tickets. He's one of the players in the league that sells tickets and you know we desperately need him in our game. >> Yeah. Don't we kind of need him with the Penguins. >> Well, I live in Florida. I'd like to see him there, but people in Edmonton don't want him to leave. >> Yeah. People in Edmonton are going to be pissed that you said it with me. They just think that I'm uh obviously >> I think he's I think he's in Main State Edmonton. He likes it there. The organization is a good organization and they got a chance every year to win and that's all he wants. And I I don't see Connor leaving Edmonton. >> What? Bousard had five points last night, I think, to start the entire Yeah, pretty good for the Edmonton Oilers last night. If they don't >> I think he's the I think he's the first guy to get a hat-tick as a defenseman in game one since Mark How. And I think there was a guy in 1919 that did it also first game of the year as a defenseman. So he's in pretty good company with Mark How. >> Yeah, I'd say pretty good company. Hatrick and two assists. So I mean we're we're a part of everything. Absolute magic. with a long stick back there. Evson Oilers don't win one though again. >> I mean, it's every offseason, every end of season, it's like McDavid, we want to see him, we want to see him, we want to see him. Hopefully, they're able to get it done for the good of the sport. Another Go ahead. >> I I think the thing I've said on TV the last few years, they've been to two Stanley Cup finals. And the thing I've said, and this is what I've hearing out of the new coaching staff, that you need a third and fourth line, that you need a second power play unit. And you know, one line or one guy can't win a championship. You've got to have 20 guys pulling on the same rope. And I think that's what this coaching staff is going to bring into that team is this is going to be a way better team come February than it is in October. >> Let's talk about another Canadian team who's been hyped up crazy and hasn't won. Go ahead, Con man. >> Yeah, Wayne know obviously pass talking about the Toronto Maple Leafs. It's been pretty ugly, but they got the number one pick, Gavin McKenna. He made his debut last night. What' you think about it? Did you expect it to be what it was? Bill Knander goes out there, scores a goal right away, but what do you think about the Maple Leafs chances and Gavin McKenna this year? >> Well, listen, they're in a rebuilding process. Um, there's no question when you get the first pick overall. That means you didn't have a very good year the year before. But my hat goes off to this young man. You know, it's one thing to go to Toronto and be the first pick overall. And there's way more pressure if you're a Canadian boy and you get drafted in number one by Canada in Toronto. and I've listened to a lot of what he said. I've listened to him talk. He seems like he's very mature for 18 years old. Hey, listen. It's going to take a little bit of time. He's a young kid. He's not very big, but he's going to grow and get bigger and stronger. But I really like the way he's handled himself uh with the media and with the game itself. He's going to be fine. And I think that the the group in Toronto has put together a nice little little hockey club here. I think they're going to be a better team this year than people anticipate. I uh I hope that for their fans and they they're viewed as what the Dallas Cowboys of Canada, right? Always hyp. >> Yeah. The Yankees. Yankees of baseball, the Cowboys of of football. It's very similar. It's you know, people love the Toronto Maple Leafs. It's it's in Canada. We used to only have two teams. So in the 40s, 50s, and 60s, all you watched was either Toronto or Montreal. And so they have this huge following right across the entire country. >> Is Austin still up there? is I heard all the Americans want to get the hell out of Canada. What's that all about? >> No, that that's not true. U Austin I think really likes it there. He gets treated great. He's a great player. Um I don't think it's all the Americans wanted to leave Canada. It's just sometimes business comes into play, right? And you know for Brady Tuk, he probably wanted to play with his brother. Why not? And so just happens that he's American boy. >> Yeah, it just so happens. Yeah, I agree. whenever I got a chance to see him at that Rams game sitting down. What a >> hilarious situation by the way. Thank you for the invite up there. Drinks were fantastic. Stories were legendary and obviously sitting right behind Demar D Rozan and Russell Westbrook and then you know everybody it's just Wayne Gretzky's here. First thing I say is hey all the Americans are trying to get the hell out of Canada. He goes no no no don't say that don't don't say that. I go that's what I'm reading. I'm reading all the headlines. They said get me the hell out of this country. There you go. Don't don't. This has been happening for a long time. It's business. We understand how this goes. Like immediately was like do not I appreciate you having to take that stance or taking that stance, but >> yeah, they they need to watch Shores. Best show on TV. >> The Canadians have such good lingo. >> Canadians are a funny bunch, bro. You guys are a funny bunch.
